jobs.title: Outbound Email Copywriter (BBS895)
jobs.excerpt: We're looking for an Outbound Email Copywriter to devise and write cold email campaigns for a fast-growing B2B sales intelligence platform serving GTM teams that sell into local and vertical SMB markets.
jobs.description:
We're looking for an Outbound Email Copywriter to devise and write cold email campaigns for a fast-growing B2B sales intelligence platform serving GTM teams that sell into local and vertical SMB markets. You will own the strategy and execution of outbound email campaigns, researching ICPs and pain points, building copy angles, writing sequences that get opened and replied to, and optimizing based on results.

This is a writing-first role. You need substantial B2B outbound email experience, ideally across a wide variety of SMB verticals. You should know how to research an ICP, identify pain points that actually land, build a compelling copy angle, structure a proper sequence, and A/B test your way to better performance over time. Past campaign results are required to apply. You will be working inside the company's own in-house platform, which combines a database of businesses and contact information with an enrichment tool that functions similarly to Clay, allowing you to create customized research variables per prospect. You will also use general AI tools and web research to inform personalization and messaging. If you have the experience, can show the results, and want to own outbound campaign copy for a fast-growing B2B platform, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires availability during US business hours
  • Work inside a fast-growing B2B sales intelligence platform with real traction and a growing SMB-focused client base
  • Access to a proprietary in-house enrichment platform with deep prospect data and customizable research variables
  • High-ownership copywriting role with direct impact on pipeline generation and campaign performance

What You'll Work On

ICP Research and Copy Strategy

  • Research ICPs, pain points, and buying triggers across a wide range of SMB verticals including HVAC, dental, restaurants, and others
  • Build copy angles that speak directly to real prospect problems rather than generic value propositions
  • Use the company's in-house enrichment platform to build customized research variables per prospect and leverage them for meaningful personalization
  • Use general AI tools and web research to deepen prospect understanding and sharpen messaging

Sequence Writing and Campaign Execution

  • Write proper cold email sequences from subject line through follow-ups that generate opens, replies, and meetings
  • Structure sequences with the right cadence, tone, and escalation logic for each vertical and ICP
  • Develop and test multiple messaging angles per campaign to identify what resonates best
  • Manage multiple active campaigns simultaneously without losing quality or attention to detail

A/B Testing and Optimization

  • A/B test subject lines, opening lines, CTAs, and sequence structures systematically
  • Analyze campaign performance data including open rates, reply rates, and positive response rates and use it to improve copy
  • Identify what is working across campaigns and apply learnings quickly to new sequences
  • Flag underperforming campaigns early and propose specific copy changes to improve results

Collaboration and Documentation

  • Work closely with the GTM and sales team to align email messaging with broader campaign goals and ICP priorities
  • Maintain organized campaign documentation including copy versions, test results, and performance notes

What You Bring

  • Substantial B2B outbound email experience with a track record of campaigns that generated real replies and meetings across a variety of SMB verticals — this is the primary requirement
  • Ability to research an ICP, identify genuine pain points, and build copy angles that land rather than generic pitches
  • Knows how to structure a proper cold email sequence and understands cadence, tone, and escalation logic
  • Strong A/B testing discipline with the ability to optimize campaigns based on real performance data rather than gut feel
  • Past campaign results to show — open rates, reply rates, meetings booked, or similar metrics are required to apply
  • Comfortable working inside a proprietary enrichment or research platform and using custom prospect data to inform personalization
  • Comfortable using AI tools and web research as part of the research and writing process
  • Excellent written English with a direct, concise, and human communication style

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Clay or a similar prospect enrichment and research platform
  • Background in outbound sales or SDR work that gives you firsthand understanding of what buyers respond to
  • Experience writing cold email for a B2B SaaS, sales intelligence, or data platform
  • Familiarity with cold email tools such as Instantly, Smartlead, or Apollo

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. Past campaign results showing performance metrics such as open rates, reply rates, or meetings booked — this is required to apply and candidates without results to share will not be considered
  3. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing your B2B outbound email experience, and walking through one campaign you built from ICP research through to results

Only candidates who submit both campaign results and a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you have substantial B2B outbound email experience, can research an ICP and turn it into a campaign that actually converts, and want to own cold email copy for a fast-growing B2B platform with real traction in the SMB market, this role gives you the ownership and the direct impact to do your best work.

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record an video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

jobs.title: Executive Creative Director
jobs.excerpt: About Oxford Road Oxford Road is the world’s largest podcast advertising agency.
jobs.description:
About Oxford Road

Oxford Road is the world’s largest podcast advertising agency. We unite brands and creators through strategy and technology for outcomes only we can deliver.

Since the beginning of podcasting, we’ve been here building the playbook, setting the standards, and scaling brands through the power of audio and creator-driven media. Today, we manage campaigns across podcasts, radio, streaming audio, YouTube, and emerging creator platforms for clients that include half of the top advertisers in podcasting.

What really sets us apart? We’re not just buying media. We’re shaping the market itself.

Our thought leadership defines the conversation. Our newsletter reaches thousands of industry decision-makers every week. Our podcast, The Media Roundtable, convenes the most influential voices in audio advertising. Our annual Chief Audio Officer Summit is the premier gathering for marketers, platforms, and creators shaping the future of the medium. Our research (from attribution methodologies to brand safety frameworks) becomes industry standard.

We don’t wait for the market to tell us what’s next. We build it.

The Role

The Executive Creative Director is Oxford Road's most senior creative leader, accountable for the quality, performance, and culture of everything the Creative department produces across host-read, pre-produced audio, and bespoke 360-degree campaigns. This role owns the creative standard across every client account, not just the highest-profile ones, and is responsible for ensuring that standard is consistently met, measurably tied to results, and strengthened by every test the team runs.

This is a leadership role built around three commitments: quality on everything that ships, creative tied to performance, and testing built in as a standard practice rather than an afterthought. The ECD is the keeper of the craft and the driver of the creative department's contribution to client outcomes, agency growth, and new business.

Scope of Ownership

  • Owns creative quality end-to-end across all client accounts: reviewing work in flight before it ships, closing the feedback loop to writers directly, and maintaining a consistent standard across host-read and pre-produced disciplines
  • Owns how Audiolytics is used across the department: as a benchmark and coaching tool integrated with compliance and performance data, not as a checkbox exercise
  • Owns the talent onboarding, briefing, and feedback process: ensuring every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time
  • Owns the connection between creative output and market performance: working with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines and translate results into creative direction
  • Owns a test-and-learn culture in partnership with Analytics: bringing creative hypotheses, making testing a standard part of how briefs are written, and ensuring what the team learns shapes the next round of work
  • Owns the full creative team: leading and developing writers across Bespoke and Format tiers and producers across host-read and pre-produced disciplines
  • Owns key client and talent relationships at the senior creative level: these relationships stay direct, not delegated
  • Owns the department's presence in new business pitches: concept development, pitch decks, and demo work, including a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles)
  • Owns creative support for bespoke, creator-first partnerships and 360-degree campaigns
  • Does not own test design, statistical analysis, or tracking infrastructure; those sit within Analytics
  • Does not own production cost, change-order pricing, or P those sit within Finance

Decision Rights

  • Final decision-maker on creative quality: what ships and what does not, across all accounts and both production disciplines
  • Owns how Audiolytics is applied, evolved, and integrated with compliance and performance data across the department
  • Authority to direct the creative team across writing and production in service of quality and performance outcomes
  • Owns casting, talent direction, and host feedback structures
  • Owns creative concept and approach for new business pitches; coordinates with account leadership on pitch strategy and timing
  • Escalates resource, capacity, and structural gaps to the Chief Executive Officer with recommendations
  • Does not make unilateral commitments on media plans, client contracts, or agency pricing

What You'll Do

Pillar 1: Quality on Everything That Ships

  • Quality control, end-to-end: Own QC across all creative that ships. Review work in flight against a clear quality bar before it reaches a client. Close the feedback loop so direction reaches writers directly. Hold host-read and pre-produced work to the distinct craft standards each discipline requires.
  • Audiolytics as benchmark, not scorecard: Own how Audiolytics is used and where it goes next. Prevent the score from becoming the goal. Integrate it with compliance and performance data to produce real insight, and drive the automation that lets it scale without adding manual burden to writers.
  • Talent onboarding and feedback: Own how talent is onboarded, briefed, and coached. Ensure every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time.

Pillar 2: Creative Tied to Performance

  • Creative performance and market outcomes: Own the connection between what ships and how it performs. Work with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines, then translate performance and Audiolytics data into creative direction so outcomes, not just compliance, shape decisions on every account.
  • Closing the loop: Ensure what the team learns in market changes how they write, cast, and coach. Every round of creative should start smarter than the last.

Pillar 3: Testing Built In

  • Test-and-learn culture: Foster a team that is curious about what is working, what is not, and why. Analytics owns statistical design and tracking infrastructure; this role brings the creative hypotheses and ensures what the team learns shapes the next brief.
  • Test-ready briefs: Make a clear hypothesis and planned variants a standard part of how briefs are written, so testing is part of the everyday process rather than a separate project.

Leading the Department

  • Team leadership and development: Lead and develop the full creative team across writing tiers (Bespoke and Format) and production disciplines (host-read and pre-produced). Shepherd the process from brief through talent-facing direction and production. Shape the team around the skills the department needs as it grows.
  • Key client and talent relationships: Serve as the senior creative point of contact for key clients and talent. These relationships remain direct, not delegated. Clients and hosts should know who owns the creative point of view on their business.
  • New business and pitch support: Own the department's presence in every pitch: concept development, decks, and demo work. Develop and maintain a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles) so account teams walk into every pitch with real creative options.
  • Bespoke and creator-first partnerships: Own creative support for bespoke, creator-first campaigns: the 360-degree work that links show content, social, newsletters, and onsite activation to a client's brand.
  • Agency direction: Surface new formats, offerings, and creative opportunities as they emerge from the work. Bring them to leadership with a clear point of view.

Operating Cadence

  • Weekly: QC review across active accounts with creative on the agenda; one-on-ones with Bespoke and Format writing leads and Producers; cross-functional check-ins with Compliance and Analytics on Audiolytics integration, performance outcomes, and the testing roadmap; pitch and new business support as it arises; ongoing talent feedback touchpoints
  • Monthly: Performance and test result review with Analytics; talent feedback loop assessment; pitch win rate and new business creative review
  • Quarterly: Creative department performance review with leadership; Audiolytics integration and automation progress; test-and-learn record review; team development and capacity assessment

What Success Looks Like

Quality

  • Consistent creative quality across every account, with in-market creative meeting the 90% Audiolytics target
  • A measurable shift away from Audiolytics-as-checkbox behavior, without losing substantiation or compliance discipline
  • Fast turnaround on host-read work and fire drills without a drop in craft

Performance

  • Performance baselines established on priority accounts within the first 90 days
  • A growing share of active accounts with creative decisions informed by performance data and test results, not just Audiolytics compliance scores
  • Measurable performance lift on accounts where creative direction changed based on results

Testing

  • A meaningful share of active accounts running at least one creative test per quarter
  • A shared test-and-learn record that the team actively uses when briefing new work

Leadership and Growth

  • Client and talent satisfaction with the department's creative involvement and responsiveness
  • Pitch win rate and the quality of creative options the team brings to new business
  • A creative team that is developing, retained, and clear on what great looks like

Specific targets will be confirmed within the first 90 days, once performance baselines are established.

Key Performance Indicators

Creative Quality

  • Audiolytics score compliance: percentage of in-market creative meeting the 90% target
  • QC turnaround: creative reviewed before client delivery, not after, with no material exceptions
  • Host-read turnaround speed on fire drills and standard requests, within defined SLA

Performance and Testing

  • Share of active accounts with established performance baselines
  • Share of active accounts with creative decisions informed by performance or test data, growing quarter-over-quarter
  • Share of active accounts running at least one creative test per quarter
  • Test-and-learn record adoption: frequency with which the shared record informs new briefs

Leadership

  • Pitch win rate on new business opportunities where Creative is involved
  • Creative team retention and development: direct reports growing in capability and remaining engaged
  • Client and talent satisfaction with creative quality and responsiveness

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidates will bring:

  • 10 or more years of experience in creative leadership, with a track record of owning creative quality across multiple accounts or productions simultaneously
  • Deep fluency in audio advertising: host-read, pre-produced, and bespoke formats; candidates with strong audio or podcast creative backgrounds are strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to connect creative decisions to measurable performance outcomes; comfort working with data, analytics teams, and test-and-learn frameworks as inputs to creative direction
  • Experience leading and developing creative teams across writing and production disciplines; a coach and standard-setter, not just a practitioner
  • Strong point of view on what makes audio creative work: clarity of message, authenticity of voice, structure that converts; able to articulate and transfer that standard to a team
  • Experience owning or contributing to new business pitches: concept development, creative presentation, and demo work in high-stakes settings
  • Comfort working directly with talent: onboarding hosts, providing structured feedback, and maintaining creative relationships at the senior level
  • A bias toward ownership: someone who runs toward gaps, raises the standard without being asked, and holds the quality bar even under deadline pressure

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a hands-on copywriting role for every account. The ECD sets the standard, resources the team, and steps in personally on the highest-stakes work. Writing every script is not the job.
  • Not a testing infrastructure role. Analytics owns test design, statistical analysis, tracking, and reporting mechanics. This role owns what gets tested, why, and what the team does with the results.
  • Not a pricing or P&L role. Finance owns production cost, change-order pricing, and the margin conversation. Creative owns the work itself.
  • Not a media strategy or buying role. Those functions sit within Media. The ECD operates within the creative lane and coordinates with Media as needed.

Key Relationships

  • Chief Executive Officer: Direct reporting relationship; accountable for creative department quality, team performance, and strategic creative direction
  • President: Coordinates on agency-wide creative positioning, new business strategy, and client escalations
  • Analytics Team: Primary partner on performance data, Audiolytics integration, test design, and the test-and-learn record
  • Compliance Team: Coordinates on script substantiation, IO requirements, and the integration of compliance signal into creative coaching
  • Account and Client Growth Teams: Partners on pitch creative, client QBRs, and performance-based creative direction conversations
  • Creator Partnerships: Coordinates on bespoke, creator-first campaigns and 360-degree deal creative
  • Finance: Coordinates on production resource needs; does not own pricing or P&L

Why This Role Matters

Creative is not a cost center at Oxford Road. It is one of the primary drivers of whether clients get results and stay. Every script that ships without a clear value proposition, every host-read that lands flat, every campaign that cannot be connected to measurable outcomes is a missed opportunity to prove what this agency can do. The Executive Creative Director is accountable for ensuring that does not happen, consistently, across every account, not just the ones leadership is watching. A strong ECD means clients win faster, advocacy compounds, and new business is easier to win. Without it, the agency's creative output is only as good as whoever happened to review it last.

The pay range for this role is: $170-210k USD base + incentive plan

jobs.description:
SAP TM S/4HANA Rollout Consultant, United Kingdom

Contract: 6 months initially, extensible. Long-term programme. Start: 1 November 2026 Location: Remote, for consultants based in the United Kingdom. Day rate: GBP 400 a day, inside IR35. Language: English.

The programme

A global manufacturing organisation is moving its transportation processes onto SAP Transportation Management (TM) on S/4HANA. The global template is the base, and it is being rolled out to sites in waves. Each wave brings new plants, new carriers and new country requirements into the template.

You will own the TM solution for the waves you are given. You will run fit-to-standard sessions with the business, decide what the template already covers and what is a real local gap, and design the answer without breaking the global standard. You will then carry that design through build, testing, cutover and early support after go-live.

What you will work on

Fit-gap for each rollout wave. Local transport practice, carriers, legal and document needs measured against the global design. TM solution design on S/4HANA. Freight planning, carrier selection and tendering, freight order execution, charge calculation and freight settlement. Integration across the S/4HANA logistics chain. Outbound sales orders and deliveries, inbound purchasing flows, warehouse execution, and freight cost through to finance. Carrier connectivity. EDI or business network onboarding, tracking, and status messages from carriers. Functional specifications for the build team, working closely with integration, development and test leads. Test planning and defect resolution through integration and user acceptance testing. Cutover, hypercare and handover to support for each wave. Feeding what each wave teaches back into the template, so the next wave starts from a better base.

What you bring

8 or more years in SAP logistics, with SAP TM on S/4HANA as a core part of it. At least one TM rollout or global template programme for a manufacturing business, where you did the fit-gap and the solution design yourself, not only the configuration. Working knowledge of how TM connects to SD, MM, EWM and FI/CO, and where those integrations tend to break. Experience running workshops with business users and turning what they say into a design and a specification. Comfort working remotely across countries in a programme team made up of several companies.

Useful but not essential:

SAP Business Network for Logistics, or a carrier visibility platform. Both embedded and side-by-side TM deployments. Automotive, industrial or process manufacturing. Multimodal, international or dangerous goods transport. SAP TM certification.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent TM rollout: the countries or sites in scope, whether TM was embedded or side-by-side, and what you personally designed.

jobs.title: Penetration Tester - Hardware (Canada)
jobs.excerpt: Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing.
jobs.description:
Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing. We exist to eliminate the false sense of security that comes from shallow testing and checkbox-driven assessments. Our slogan, "Ready for more than a VA scan?", reflects a simple standard: real security work should be rigorous, manual, and built to uncover what automated approaches miss. Our clients span government, technology, law enforcement, retail, healthcare, and financial services, and they rely on us because credibility matters when the stakes are high.

Packetlabs is looking for an Penetration Tester - Hardware to lead security assessments of embedded and IoT devices, the physical products where a vulnerability lives in silicon, firmware, and board layout, rather than in a web request. The Ethical Hacker - Hardware is a specialized technical role focused on assessing embedded systems across all industries, from consumer IoT to industrial and connected devices. This role involves getting hands-on with a device, opening it up, and proving what an attacker with physical or local access can really do.

This role requires the rare combination of offensive security instinct and genuine hardware fundamentals. You will work directly with clients to understand their devices and deliver findings that improve security posture.

Who we are looking for

  • No egos, ever. Egos don't belong at Packetlabs. The more you learn, the less you know. You stay humble, ask questions, and work to help clients improve their security.
  • Customer-first mentality. You are an excellent communicator with clients, project managers, and teammates. You are responsive, reliable, and professional throughout every engagement.
  • You deliver work that you take pride in. Your work is an autograph of your excellence. You hold yourself to a high standard, and it shows in what you produce.
  • Digs deeper into every finding. You don't stop until impact is proven, while understanding that restraint is the right call in sensitive OT environments where high-risk activity is not appropriate.
  • Comfortable being uncomfortable. You move toward obstacles, not away from them. Consulting is not a typical job and requires adapting to rapidly changing environments.
  • Always learning. Cybersecurity changes every day, and you keep up because you want to. You are deeply aware of your skillset and committed to improving it.
  • Self-motivated and dependable. You take ownership of your work and your outcomes without needing to be managed into them.

What you’ll be doing

  • Hardware Penetration Testing
    • Plan and execute end-to-end hardware penetration tests on embedded and IoT devices, against a defined scope and rules of engagement
    • Identify, access, and exploit on-board debug interfaces: JTAG, SWD, UART, and similar, to gain code execution or memory access
    • Extract firmware via debug ports, in-circuit flash reads (SPI / I2C / NAND), or chip-off when required, and analyze it for vulnerabilities
    • Intercept and analyze data on common embedded buses (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, USB) using logic analyzers and protocol decoders
    • Where in scope, perform side-channel analysis and fault injection (power analysis, voltage/clock glitching) to bypass secure boot, readout protection, or authentication
  • Firmware Analysis & Reverse Engineering
    • Reverse engineer firmware and embedded binaries (Ghidra, IDA, Binwalk, etc.) to find logic flaws, hardcoded secrets, and exploitable conditions
    • Assess physical attack surface, tamper resistance, and key/secret storage
    • Distinguish between theoretical and operationally relevant risk to keep findings actionable
  • Client Advisory & Remediation
    • Write high-quality technical reports and present findings to client stakeholders, both technical and non-technical
    • Advise on practical, prioritized remediation that clients can act on
    • Build client confidence through credibility, clear communication, and proven impact
  • Methodology, Research & Continuous Improvement
    • Build and maintain lab tooling, test rigs, and internal methodology
    • Contribute to research, responsible disclosure, and internal knowledge-sharing
    • Stay current on hardware attack techniques, embedded architectures, and defensive controls
    • Help raise the standard of hardware security work across the firm

What success looks like

  • Clients gain a clear, accurate understanding of their hardware risk, backed by proven, reproducible impact
  • Findings are credible, actionable, and land for both technical and leadership audiences
  • Engagements are delivered to a consistently high standard with strong client confidence
  • Scope and rules of engagement are managed well as engagements evolve, with risk surfaced early and clearly
  • Packetlabs' hardware testing methodology and lab capability continue to mature through your contribution
  • Clients trust Packetlabs as the partner that can break their hardware before someone else does

Education and Experience

  • A graduate of an Information Security, Computer Science, or Computer/Electrical Engineering degree program (or equivalent hands-on experience)
  • Strong electronics fundamentals. Able to read schematics and datasheets and reason about a board from them
  • Hands-on soldering ability, including surface-mount (SMD) rework and basic chip removal
  • Demonstrated experience accessing debug interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART) and extracting firmware from real devices
  • Comfort with core bench instruments: logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and multimeter
  • Firmware reverse-engineering skills and scripting proficiency in Python, plus enough C to read embedded code
  • Familiarity with common embedded architectures (ARM/Cortex-M, MIPS, AVR, RISC-V) and RTOS/bare-metal concepts
  • Clear written and verbal communication.
  • Nice to have (one or more would be an asset):
    • Side-channel / fault-injection experience (e.g., ChipWhisperer)
    • RF and wireless work: SDR, BLE, sub-GHz, Wi-Fi
    • Knowledge of secure boot chains, TEEs, secure elements, and HSMs
    • PCB design familiarity (KiCad / Altium) for understanding target boards
    • Published CVEs, conference talks, CTF placements, or open-source tooling
    • Relevant certifications (e.g., OSCP for breadth, or hardware-focused training)

Why us?

  • The opportunity to work on high-stakes hardware engagements where your judgment and bench skills genuinely matter
  • Receive immediate and ongoing offensive security training, mentorship, and professional development to advance your technical capabilities
  • Play a key role in shaping the growth, direction, and methodology of Packetlabs' expanding hardware practice
  • A leadership team that values substance, quality, and disciplined execution
  • Collaboration with a highly skilled team of security professionals who are passionate about technical excellence and raising the bar
  • Competitive compensation and growth opportunity
  • Flexible work environment that empowers employees to do their best work
  • Fully remote within Canada

jobs.description:
Build and run the GHL systems that turn leads into members and keep members coming back — and be the go-to support for the gym team using them.

About the Role

Seamless Assist places AI-fluent virtual assistants with growing businesses and builds the automation systems they run. We are hiring a GoHighLevel Specialist on behalf of our client, a US-based gym business. This is a fully remote role open to candidates based in South Africa.

The gym runs its lead follow-up, trial bookings, member communication, and retention campaigns through GoHighLevel. This hire owns that platform end to end — building the automations that drive memberships and supporting the owner and front-desk team who use it every day.

Culture: owner-led, fast-moving fitness business. Clear ownership, proactive communication, and steady improvement over perfection.

Role Details

  • Industry: Health & Fitness — Gym
  • Reports to: Gym Owner
  • Type: Full-time · 40 hours/week
  • Hours: US Eastern Time (EST) business hours
  • Rate: TBD
  • Location: Remote — South Africa
  • Tools: GoHighLevel (GHL), Zapier / Make / n8n, gym management software (e.g., Mindbody, ABC Glofox, PushPress, Zen Planner), Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Google Workspace

Role Overview

Every lead, trial, and member touchpoint at the gym runs through GoHighLevel. The GHL Specialist will design and maintain those systems — from the first ad inquiry to the membership renewal — and provide responsive, first-line support to the gym owner and staff.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move between building and supporting in the same day: fixing a broken trial-booking workflow in the morning, walking the front desk through the pipeline after lunch, and documenting both so it doesn't happen twice. The right person treats every support request as a signal of what to systematize next.

Key Responsibilities

GHL Automation & Build

  • Build and maintain lead nurture workflows — speed-to-lead SMS/email, trial class and intro session booking, and follow-up for leads who don't book
  • Automate the member journey — class and appointment reminders, no-show follow-up, new-member onboarding, and milestone check-ins
  • Run retention and reactivation campaigns — lapsed and frozen members, expiring memberships, failed payments, and win-back offers
  • Set up and manage pipelines, calendars, forms, surveys, landing pages/funnels, custom fields, and tags
  • Build and send email and SMS campaigns — promotions, challenges, events, and monthly member newsletters
  • Automate review requests and referral campaigns to grow the gym's reputation
  • Integrate GHL with the gym's management software, payment tools, and ad lead sources (Facebook/Instagram lead forms) via native integrations, Zapier, Make, n8n, or webhooks

Customer Support

  • Serve as first-line GHL support for the gym owner and front-desk/sales staff
  • Manage and respond to member and lead inquiries in the GHL Conversations inbox (SMS, email, social DMs) within agreed response times
  • Troubleshoot issues: broken workflows, failed sends, calendar sync errors, A2P/10DLC and email deliverability problems, integration failures
  • Train gym staff on using GHL — pipelines, conversations, booking, and reporting — through live walkthroughs and short recorded videos
  • Escalate billing, platform-level bugs, or out-of-scope requests to the gym owner with a clear summary

Reporting, Documentation & Improvement

  • Build dashboards that track leads, trial bookings, show rates, conversions to membership, and retention
  • Write SOPs and how-to guides for every recurring build and support issue
  • Audit the account for broken, duplicate, or unused workflows and recommend clean-up
  • Track recurring issues and propose automations or fixes that remove them at the source
  • Use AI tools to speed up campaign copy, troubleshooting, and documentation

Who Will Succeed

"Builds it right, explains it simply, and fixes the root cause — not just the ticket."

  • Has built real GHL automations for live businesses — ideally gyms, studios, or other membership businesses
  • Understands how a gym makes money: leads, trials, memberships, retention
  • Patient and clear with busy, non-technical owners and staff — explains a workflow without jargon
  • Systems thinker who documents as they go and hates fixing the same problem twice
  • Takes initiative — spots what is broken or missing and raises it before the owner does

Experience & Skills

Required

  • GHL expertise: 2+ years of hands-on GoHighLevel experience building workflows, pipelines, funnels, and campaigns for live businesses
  • Customer support: 1+ year providing customer or technical support (tickets, live chat, calls, or client success)
  • Integrations: Working knowledge of Zapier, Make, n8n, or webhooks to connect GHL with other tools
  • AI fluency: Actively uses AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) to build, write, and troubleshoot faster — specific tools and use cases confirmed at screening
  • Time zone compatibility: Able to work US Eastern Time (EST) business hours from South Africa
  • Strong communication: Exceptional written and spoken English — clear, friendly, and concise with owners, staff, and members; assessed at screening
  • Deliverability: Understanding of email and SMS deliverability, including A2P 10DLC registration
  • Remote setup: Reliable high-speed internet and a dedicated workspace

Preferred

  • Experience with gyms, fitness studios, or other membership-based businesses
  • Experience with gym management software (Mindbody, ABC Glofox, PushPress, Zen Planner, or similar)
  • GHL Admin certification
  • Familiarity with GHL Conversation AI / AI Employee features
  • Experience running Facebook/Instagram lead-gen campaigns into GHL

We are looking for a Senior Google CCAIP Engineer to build, configure, and test customer contact center solutions on Google's Contact Center AI (CCAI) Platform. The role focuses on implementing approved business and technical specifications, including DTMF IVR menus, call flows, queue configurations, and routing logic. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience configuring cloud contact center platforms in production environments and can ensure accurate implementation, thorough testing, and clear technical documentation.

Responsibilities

  • Build and configure DTMF IVR menu structures in Google CCAI Platform, including menu hierarchies, keypad mappings, prompt sequences, and navigation logic.

  • Configure IVR messaging and multilingual prompts, including greetings, language selection, invalid-input handling, recording consent, after-hours messages, and overcapacity notifications.

  • Implement call flows and routing configurations, including queue assignments, fallback rules, overflow handling, callbacks, and warm and cold transfers.

  • Configure integrations with CRM systems, virtual agents, Agent Assist, and agent desktop components according to approved technical specifications.

  • Develop and execute test cases covering IVR menu paths, routing scenarios, transfers, timeouts, and edge cases; support customer user acceptance testing (UAT) and resolve configuration defects.

  • Maintain traceability between approved requirements and platform configurations, and prepare technical documentation, call flow diagrams, and operational runbooks.

  • Follow established change management and release procedures while collaborating with customer stakeholders to clarify requirements and ensure accurate implementation.

  • 5+ years of experience building and configuring IVR solutions and call flows on cloud contact center or CCaaS platforms in production environments.

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with Google Cloud Contact Center AI Platform (CCAIP)

  • Strong understanding of DTMF IVR configuration, including menu hierarchies, keypad mapping, prompt sequencing, invalid-input handling, and timeouts.

  • Experience configuring queues, routing rules, fallback mechanisms, overflow handling, callbacks, and call transfers.

  • Skills in developing custom integrations using platform APIs, webhooks, or SDKs.

  • Experience implementing conversational AI integrations with Dialogflow CX, Conversational Agents, or Agent Studio.

  • Skills in working with enterprise CRM or service management integrations, such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft Dynamics, Zendesk, or HubSpot.

  • Ability to implement approved business and technical specifications accurately and identify and escalate ambiguities or conflicting requirements.

  • Experience preparing and executing structured test cases, supporting UAT, and resolving configuration defects.

  • Ability to prepare clear technical documentation, including call flow diagrams and configuration records.

  • Experience working directly with customer technical and business stakeholders.

  • Good command of English, both written and spoken.

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge of telephony protocols and technologies, including SIP, SIPREC, call recording, or quality management integrations.

  • Experience with additional CCaaS platforms, such as Genesys Cloud CX, Amazon Connect, NICE CXone, or Five9.

  • Experience delivering contact center solutions in regulated environments with strict audit and change management requirements.

  • Experience delivering multilingual contact center solutions, including English/French environments.

We offer:

  • Culture of Relentless Performance: join an unstoppable technology development team with a 99% project success rate and more than 30% year-over-year revenue growth.
  • Competitive Pay and Benefits: enjoy a comprehensive compensation and benefits package, including health insurance, and a relocation program.
  • Work From Anywhere Culture: make the most of the flexibility that comes with remote work.
  • Growth Mindset: reap the benefits of a range of professional development opportunities, including certification programs, mentorship and talent investment programs, internal mobility and internship opportunities.
  • Global Impact: collaborate on impactful projects for top global clients and shape the future of industries.
  • Welcoming Multicultural Environment: be a part of a dynamic, global team and thrive in an inclusive and supportive work environment with open communication and regular team-building company social events.
  • Social Sustainability Values: join our sustainable business practices focused on five pillars, including IT education, community empowerment, fair operating practices, environmental sustainability, and gender equality.

* Miratech is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status under applicable law.

Miratech helps visionaries change the world. We are a global IT services and consulting company that brings together enterprise and start-up innovation. Today, we support digital transformation for some of the world's largest enterprises. By partnering with both large and small players, we stay at the leading edge of technology, remain nimble even as a global leader, and create technology that helps our clients further enhance their business. We are a values-driven organization and our culture of Relentless Performance has enabled over 99% of Miratech's engagements to succeed by meeting or exceeding our scope, schedule, and/or budget objectives since our inception in 1989.
Miratech has coverage across 5 continents and operates in over 25 countries around the world. Miratech retains nearly 1000 full-time professionals, and our annual growth rate exceeds 25%.

jobs.title: Sales Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Proximie is on a mission to improve healthcare by transforming the world’s operating rooms into connected ecosystems of people, devices, and data.
jobs.description:
Proximie is on a mission to improve healthcare by transforming the world’s operating rooms into connected ecosystems of people, devices, and data.

Our Intelligence Suite transforms operating room (OR) performance, keeping teams in sync and workflows on track to maximise throughput. Simultaneously our computer vision and AI capabilities capture real-time data and detect surgical events – improving quality of data outputs. The result: ORs are optimised like never before – with predictive analytics and automated notifications ensuring patients and staff are in the right place at the right time.

Once practitioners are in the OR, our Surgical Suite enables real-time remote access and creates a secure video record of every procedure; improving training, education, and collaboration. It is an intuitive asset which helps instil a culture of continuous learning, accelerates the adoption of cutting-edge medical devices, and enhances surgical performance across the entire global workforce – improving outcomes and saving lives.

Proximie was commercialised in 2019 and is available in over 500 facilities globally.

Check out our Founder and CEO Nadine’s Origins Story here:

Position Overview

Proximie is seeking a Sales Engineer to serve as the technical bridge between our commercial team and our engineering and product organizations. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role for someone who thrives on translating complex technical concepts into clear, confident conversations. This role will be critical to Proximie’s growth in the US market, supporting the commercial team as we respond to RFPs, navigate complex enterprise sales cycles, and onboard new health system partners.

Responsibilities

  • Act as the primary technical resource during the sales cycle, joining commercial conversations to address deep product, software, networking, and integration questions.

  • Lead technical discovery conversations with hospital IT, innovation teams, and procurement stakeholders covering topics such as SSO configuration, network requirements, hardware setup, cloud architecture, and data flow.

  • Translate customer requirements into clearly scoped questions or change requests for engineering and product teams.

  • Build and maintain a strong partnership with Engineering, serving as the connective tissue between field insights and internal technical teams to ensure customer needs are understood, prioritized, and addressed effectively.

  • Troubleshoot integration and configuration issues in the field, identifying root causes and driving resolution.

  • Proactively identify recurring technical friction points across deals and escalate patterns to product and engineering to inform the roadmap.

  • Support the onboarding of new health system customers by bridging the handoff between sales and implementation.

  • Maintain clear documentation of technical configurations, customer environments, and common integration patterns.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in a Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or Technical Pre-Sales role, ideally in a SaaS or health tech environment.

  • Strong foundational knowledge of networking and infrastructure, including hospital or clinical network environments (VLANs, firewalls, SSO/SAML, Active Directory).

  • Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and how cloud-based software integrates with on-premises hospital systems.

  • Ability to get into a system, understand what is happening, and fix what is configurable — you do not need to be a developer, but you need to be comfortable at the configuration and troubleshooting layer.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; you will be speaking with innovation leaders, IT directors, and C-suite stakeholders.

  • Strong judgment: you know when to say yes, when to say not yet, and how to position both in a way that builds trust.

  • Experience working in fast-moving, commercial environments where deals are complex and timelines are tight.

  • Comfortable operating without a playbook; you can figure out what questions to ask and find a path forward in ambiguous situations

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting sales in a healthcare or medtech environment.

  • Familiarity with surgical workflows, clinical documentation, or OR technology.

  • Background working with enterprise IT procurement and RFP processes.

  • Existing relationships within hospital innovation, IT, or digital health teams.

Why Work for Proximie?

  • You will be encouraged to grow in your role, take ownership and gain responsibilities. Proximie’s values are Ownership, Deliver Results, Build Trust and Go Beyond.

  • Generous annual leave. Two “well-being” days per year plus the day off for your birthday.

  • “Summer Fridays” – early office closing on Fridays during summer months.

  • Annual bonus programme – based on individual contribution.

  • To support your professional growth, all permanent employees will have access to an annual stipend of £1,000 to assist with personal development activities.

  • Flexible working hours - we trust our people to manage their time and to focus on wider results.

  • A flat organizational structure where every opinion matters, ideas are cultivated, and innovation is encouraged.

  • Proximie is a truly global company with teams across the UK, Europe, United States and the Middle East with that you will have opportunities to see the world.

Proximie is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. jobs.excerpt: About the RoleConcurrences is building the world's first AI research engine for antitrust law.
jobs.description:
About the Role

Concurrences is building the world's first AI research engine for antitrust law. We need someone with strong legal foundations who wants to own entire legal domains — designing what "correct" means, building the evaluation frameworks, and catching the subtle errors only a trained legal mind can spot. October 2026 production launch.

You'll work directly with our founder Nicolas Charbit (20 years building Concurrences into the definitive antitrust platform), our CTO Anton, and the wider Concurrences team of competition law partners and editors. Mentorship, feedback, and full access to Concurrences' 20-year case law database from day one.

Concurrences.com: The canonical antitrust platform since 2004. 100k+ articles, 20 years of case law, 120+ countries, ~50,000 professionals. Editorial board includes William Kovacic (former FTC Chair) and Mario Monti (former EU Commissioner). Now building Concurrences.AI — powering Claude, ChatGPT, and enterprise copilots to research competition law correctly.

What You'll Do

  • Evaluate AI outputs for legal accuracy across jurisdictions — EU, US, French, Brazilian enforcement

  • Build evaluation rubrics, annotation guidelines, and testing protocols for your legal domains

  • Design instructions that help the AI reason about antitrust with precision, not generic legal chat

  • Run structured experiments: "Find cases where precedent reversed." "Compare EU vs. US on vertical restraints."

  • Own specific domains end-to-end — EU merger control, cartels, abuse of dominance — and shape the product roadmap from domain insight

  • Write evaluation scripts using AI coding tools (no engineering background needed)

What You Have

  • Law degree (JD, LL.B., or equivalent) with strong academic record. Antitrust coursework, thesis, research, or internship is a plus — but solid legal training combined with genuine interest in learning competition law is what matters most

  • 0-2 years professional experience welcome, not required

  • You've used Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM and have a sense for where they struggle

  • Strong English writing. French is a plus but not required

  • You're curious about AI + law and want to be part of defining how AI serves legal research

Compensation

€1,200–€2,400/month depending on experience and output, paid in EUR via Wise. Independent contractor, monthly invoicing.

Fully remote. Async-first with regular mentoring sessions. Learn competition law and AI evaluation on the job — we invest in your growth. Start: ASAP.

Tardus Wealth Strategies

Remote | 1099 Independent Contractor | 100% Uncapped Commission | Residual Income

Build your own pipeline and book of business

This is a 100% commission role with no base salary. You are responsible for generating your own pipeline. Company-supported opportunities may supplement your efforts, but this role is not a fit for candidates who rely on inbound leads or a company filling out their calendar.

About Tardus

Tardus Wealth Strategies helps individuals work toward sustainable cash flow and long-term wealth through a structured, consultative approach. We believe how you sell matters as much as what you sell. Our clients trust us with important financial decisions, and we take that responsibility seriously.

Who thrives here

We welcome professionals with a track record of creating and closing their own opportunities, particularly independent insurance producers, door-to-door sales professionals, and experienced 1099 or full-commission salespeople. Real estate, mortgage, B2B business development, and consultative sales backgrounds can also translate well when paired with strong prospecting skills.

You should be comfortable initiating conversations, handling rejection professionally, asking for introductions, and maintaining consistent follow-up. Experience building a book of business matters more than having sold at a specific price point.

Prospect and own your pipeline

  • Generate qualified opportunities through direct outreach, networking, referrals, and affiliate relationships.
  • Build consistent prospecting habits and proactively schedule discovery calls and strategy sessions.
  • Expand beyond your existing network and maintain enough new activity to support ongoing production.
  • Own each opportunity from initial outreach through follow-up, enrollment, and relationship development.

Build affiliate relationships that generate leads

Developing an active affiliate and referral partner network is a core responsibility of this role. We are looking for relationship builders who can earn trust with professionals serving potential Tardus clients and turn those relationships into a consistent source of qualified introductions.

  • Identify and connect with prospective affiliates and centers of influence, including CPAs, real estate agents, mortgage professionals, insurance professionals, and business owners.
  • Initiate conversations to understand each partner’s clients, priorities, and needs. Explain who Tardus serves and where an introduction may be appropriate.
  • Build relationships through reliable communication, useful information, and follow-through—not simply requests for leads.
  • Help interested partners understand the referral process and make introductions easy using Tardus resources and established processes.
  • Maintain regular contact with affiliates, strengthen productive relationships, and continue developing new partners.
  • Follow up promptly on introductions and keep partners appropriately informed while respecting prospective clients’ privacy.
  • Track partner outreach, active relationships, referrals, appointments, and resulting enrollments in the CRM.

Success means building a network of engaged partners who understand the value of Tardus and consistently introduce qualified prospects. Collecting contacts alone is not enough.

Lead consultative sales conversations

  • Conduct virtual discovery and strategy sessions using structured, question-based methods such as SPIN or NEPQ.
  • Understand each prospect’s goals, challenges, and financial priorities before discussing potential solutions.
  • Clearly explain Tardus programs, address objections honestly, and help qualified prospects make informed decisions.
  • Enroll clients into appropriate programs and identify aligned opportunities for VIP enrollment and renewals.

Use the systems and support provided

Tardus provides a consultative sales framework, training, referral development guidance, and tools to support your efforts. You bring the initiative and consistent activity needed to create business. Company-supported opportunities are supplemental, not a guaranteed source of appointments.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, clear next steps, and timely follow-up.
  • Track prospecting, affiliate development, appointments, conversions, and revenue.
  • Participate in coaching and training, apply feedback, and continuously improve your skills.

jobs.description:
About Broadvoice

At Broadvoice, we believe that exceptional customer experience is the cornerstone of business success. Our AI-powered contact center and communications solutions are designed to help mid-market businesses simplify service, enhance satisfaction, and swiftly resolve issues.

Our holistic approach to CX sets us apart in the market. We don’t just provide software. We offer a proven CX framework backed by hands-on support. And our platform was built to be easy to deploy, intuitive to use, and scalable without chaos.

Every role in our company contributes to our mission of providing and creating exceptional experiences. Whether you’re in product, sales, support, marketing, or operations, your work directly impacts our customers and, by extension, their customers. Collaboration, innovation, and a shared commitment to excellence define our culture.

POSITION SUMMARY

Broadvoice is looking for a Sales Engineer in Madrid to be the technical voice of GoContact, our cloud contact center (CCaaS) platform, for partners and customers across Spain. You'll build and run demos, set up IVR menus, routing and queues that show a prospect what their contact center could look like, and answer the technical questions that move deals forward. You'll work closely with our sales team and channel partners and report to Christian Nieves, Sales Engineering Manager.

The hard part: every demo is rebuilt for a specific partner and prospect, and sometimes the honest answer is "not like that." You'll need the judgment to avoid promising what the product can't do, and the skill to keep the deal moving anyway.

This role is remote, based in or near Madrid, with about 20% travel within Spain to meet partners and customers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Build and deliver tailored GoContact demos for partners and prospects, remotely and in person.
  • Run technical discovery: learn how a prospect's contact center works today (channels, volumes, routing, reporting) and what isn't working.
  • Configure demo and proof-of-concept environments: IVR flows, skills-based routing, queues, overflow, after-hours handling and reporting.
  • Prepare the technical sections of proposals, RFIs and RFPs, with final solution sign-off from your manager.
  • Support partner sales reps with product training and fast, accurate technical answers so they can sell with confidence.
  • Capture customer requirements and feature requests and pass them to Product with clear context.
  • Help move stalled deals forward and hand closed deals cleanly to the implementation team.

    • QUALIFICATIONS

    What you need:

    • Hands-on experience in or supporting contact centers, for example at a BPO, a contact center technology vendor, or an in-house customer service operation. You know the metrics (service level, abandonment, handle time) and what drives them.
    • Experience configuring a contact center or telephony platform yourself: IVR menus, queues or skills, routing rules and opening hours.
    • Confidence presenting and demoing software to customers and explaining technical ideas in plain business terms.
    • Professional fluency in Spanish and English, spoken and written.
    • Good judgment when a customer asks for something the product can't do: you confirm before you commit and come back with a recommendation.
    • Enjoy working side by side with sales reps and partners, and able to travel within Spain about 20% of the time.

    Nice to have (we'll teach the rest):

    • Previous sales engineer, pre-sales or solutions consultant experience
    • Experience with GoContact
    • Experience working with channel partners or resellers
    • CRM integrations (Salesforce, Zendesk, Dynamics) or APIs
    • Portuguese

    If you meet most of the must-haves but not every one, we'd still like to hear from you.

    WHY BROADVOICE

    We're not just building communication tools; we're creating the future of connection. And we need people who want to build it with us.

    Own Your Growth
    No cookie-cutter career paths here. Sharpen your technical edge, step into leadership, or chart a course you haven't even mapped yet. You'll get real mentorship, real resources, and the autonomy to own your outcomes.

    Work on Your Terms
    Remote-first isn't a perk we bolted on, it's how we operate. We trust you to deliver, wherever you do your best work.

    A Team Built Different
    Diverse. Inclusive. Real. This is a culture that invests in people, not just performance metrics. You'll be surrounded by people who've got your back and push you to do better work.

    Impact You Can Point To
    Your ideas won't get lost in the shuffle. You'll have the backing of a product that competes well, and a direct hand in transforming Broadvoice into a CX powerhouse in the channel.

    If you're a strategic thinker who thrives on collaboration and turns ideas into results, we want to meet you. Apply now and lead the charge with us.

    Broadvoice is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. Reasonable accommodation will be made as needed for individuals with disabilities.

​

·Collaborate closely with business leaders and HR business partners to understand their specific needs and align HR practices with business objectives.

·Provide guidance and support to business leaders on employee relations matters, including performance management, disciplinary actions, grievances, reasonable accommodations and conflict resolution.

·Coach and influence HR Business Partners on interventions required for individuals, managers, and/or teams on preventing employee relations risks, effective management of performance cases, giving performance feedback, and increasing employee engagement.

·Guide HR Business Partners (HRBPs) in handling simple employee relations cases based on the employee relations hierarchy and investigation mechanisms.

·Oversee and guide employee relations activities in the North America region ensuring fair and consistent treatment of employees and compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

·Effectively manage ER cases including investigations, disciplinary issues, reasonable accommodations, interpersonal employee conflicts, under performance, involuntary exits (including reduction in force) and other employee-related matters to successful resolution.

·Serve as a trusted advisor in the employee experience by building and facilitating ER and compliance processes that emphasize fair, consistent, and respectful outcomes.

·Lead and own the end-to-end resolution of complex employee relations issues.

·Conduct reviews and investigations on sensitive workplace issues and employee relations matters.

·For severe and non-compliant employee relations cases, involve the legal department in investigations, fostering close collaboration to ensure compliance and mitigate legal risks.

·Stay current with US and Canada employment laws and regulations.

·Manage and ensure compliance with all employment law regulations, social relations and practices for countries in North America where the company operates.

·Proactively identify, manage and monitor risks and propose improvements and risk mitigation strategies.

·Interpret, communicate and maintain ER policies and processes.

·Responsible for creating regional ER policies to include updating regional North American employee handbooks.

·Partner with Legal partners to ensure company policies and practices

·Comply with applicable country and local laws and regulations.

·Recommend policy changes and enhancements based on investigation findings and emerging trends.

·Conduct periodic compliance audits to identify and address potential compliance gaps and recommend appropriate actions to mitigate risks.

·Collaborate with legal and HR teams to design and implement ER and HR compliance training programs tailored for HR, employees, and managers.

  • Documentation and Reporting:

From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

​

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Semantic Layer team in Bengaluru. You'll own the health, delivery, and growth of the team behind MetricFlow — building and coaching a group of engineers, setting technical direction in partnership with your leads, and ensuring one of the most important projects in the modern data stack keeps shipping with quality and momentum.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend most of your time growing people, running a healthy delivery process, and shaping strategy — but you'll stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make sound technical calls and earn the trust of a senior engineering team. You'll also be the steward of a public, community-facing open-source project, balancing the needs of internal roadmap and external contributors.

About the team

The Semantic Layer team owns the systems that turn dbt models into trusted, reusable business metrics. At the heart of this is MetricFlow — the open-source semantic engine that powers the dbt Semantic Layer. MetricFlow lets data teams define metrics once in code and consume them consistently across BI tools, notebooks, AI agents, and downstream applications.

This team is the steward of MetricFlow as an open-source project: shipping releases, reviewing community contributions, evolving the query compiler, and ensuring it integrates cleanly with the broader dbt ecosystem. The team works at the intersection of language design, query compilation, and distributed data execution — solving problems that directly shape how thousands of organizations measure their business.

What you'll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of software engineers building MetricFlow — hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, and day-to-day support.

  • Own delivery for the Semantic Layer team: planning, prioritization, execution, and predictable shipping of high-quality software.

  • Partner with your senior and staff engineers to set technical direction across metric definitions, query compilation, dimensional modeling, and SQL generation for multiple data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and others).

  • Steward MetricFlow as an open-source project — set the bar for how the team triages issues, reviews external pull requests, manages releases, and engages the community on GitHub and in Slack.

  • Collaborate with engineering leaders across the dbt platform, dbt Core, and the Semantic Layer service to ensure MetricFlow integrates seamlessly with the rest of the dbt ecosystem.

  • Partner with product, design, and developer-relations counterparts to translate customer and community feedback into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap.

  • Drive engineering excellence in performance, reliability, and observability of metric query execution at scale.

  • Foster a culture of design docs, thoughtful code review, and durable engineering — shipping fast without shipping sloppy.

Skills we're looking for

  • Experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, and performance management, with a track record of shipping production systems.

  • A strong engineering foundation — you've built and shipped production software yourself and can engage credibly on architecture and technical tradeoffs with a senior team.

  • Familiarity with the technical domain: SQL fundamentals, how analytical query engines and data warehouses execute queries, and systems that involve parsing, compilation, or transformation (query planners, DSL compilers, type systems, or rule-based engines).

  • Solid grasp of software design principles: clean APIs, modularity, testability, and backwards compatibility — and the judgment to hold a team to them.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication — you can explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineers, product managers, and external community members.

  • Experience leading in a distributed, asynchronous team environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience leading or contributing to a popular open-source project, including managing a community of external contributors.

  • Familiarity with dbt, MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or other semantic-layer technologies.

  • Background in data warehousing internals, query optimization, or analytical SQL dialects.

  • Experience with CI/CD, GitHub Actions, and release engineering for Python libraries.

  • Exposure to building developer-facing APIs, SDKs, or CLIs.

Why join us

  • Impact at scale: Your team's code will run inside the data platforms of tens of thousands of companies, including some of the world's largest enterprises.

  • Open-source ownership: You'll lead the team behind a foundational open-source project — visible, reviewed, and used by the global data community.

  • A team that values craft: We invest in design docs, code review, and durable engineering. We ship fast, but we don't ship sloppy.

  • Competitive compensation: Market-leading salary, equity, comprehensive health insurance, generous time off, learning and wellness stipends, and home-office support.

Perks and Benefits

  • 100% employer-paid medical insurance*
  • Generous paid time away from work, including paid vacation or flexible/unlimited vacation depending on role and country, plus paid sick time, inclusive parental leave, paid holidays, including a year-end Global Week of Rest, and volunteer days off.
  • RSU stock grants*
  • Professional development and training opportunities

  • Monthly cell phone stipend
  • Access to an innovative mental health support platform that offers personalized care and resources in areas such as: therapy, coaching, and self-guided mindfulness exercises for all covered employees and their covered dependents.

Job Title: Medical Virtual Assistant — Patient Intake, Admin & Billing
Position Type: Full-Time (40 hours per week)
