jobs.description:
Principal Engineer

College Board - Technology 

Location: This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office).

Type: This is a full-time position 

About the Team 

College Board Technology teams have a key role to play in the organization’s ability to deliver against its strategic priorities. To do this most effectively, we’ve developed a culture around a set of principles. In Technology, we are organized as teams dedicated to products. And we say products, not projects because in software, projects are subject to abandonware, but products get better over time. They get better because we wake up every day thinking about how to improve our products.

Engineers and architects at College Board exist as a group of poly skilled professionals working in swarms. And, while we may help to mentor and guide others, our critical work is to code, not manage. Our goal is to free creativity by removing dependencies between teams and we do that architecturally and infrastructurally so that one team’s innovation is not burdensome to other teams. We also make war on administrivia and context switching. This approach relies on our ability to hire, retain, and engage skilled talent.

We are committed to remaining current with new technologies, and this requires a focus on learning and development. We challenge all engineers and architects to keep learning because we know technology will not stop changing, and we are committed to supporting this growth. We’ll either fall behind or keep learning for the rest of our careers. We also know that elite technologists don’t want to work in backwaters, so we never again want to fall far behind in the technology we use.

About the Opportunity  

As the Principal Engineer, you will demonstrate success leading large, strategic, or complex areas that have clear impact to the domain. You are a highly skilled, experienced, and motivated Engineering Leader who will own setting architectural direction for a broader domain; help evolve systems toward it; and be able to influence and deliver initiatives with organizational impact and priority. Your expertiseand desire to maintain awareness and knowledge of the emerging technology trends within the industry will help support the College Board’s products.

Strategy & Design Leadership (60%)

  • Set architectural direction for domains and systems.
  • Deliver upon initiatives with organizational impact.
  • Define technical strategy that improves products, infrastructure, security, processes, and organization, while staying abreast of risks and opportunities that influence strategy.
  • Design and implement systems and frameworks that can succeed in the long-term.
  • Provide exceptional leadership and technical innovations to features that span boundaries across engineering teams.

Coaching & Collaboration (40%)

  • Be a great partner, working across technical teams to build sustainable contracts looking out for the good of system vs. what might be easiest for a sole product.
  • Work closely with development teams, product management, and other stakeholders to ensure that architecture supports the needs of all business units.
  • Foster strong working relationships with other technologists outside our team.
  • Work closely with Enterprise Architecture, DevOps, Infrastructure, and Security teams to ensure that the architecture integrates smoothly with all parts of the technology ecosystem.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence decision-making, and mentor developers.
  • Play a critical role in coaching and mentoring junior engineers.
  • Contribute content and facilitation for the Full Stack Technical Education program.
  • Support recruiting and hiring for various engineering teams and positions.

About you, you have:

  • 10+ years of experience in software systems, programming, database development, and infrastructure development and administration.
  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or similar experience with fundamentals
  • A track record of influencing and delivering initiatives with organizational impact.
  • An aptitude for directly engaging clients and users to gain strong understanding of their holistic needs.
  • An orientation towards teaching and developing junior employees.
  • A collaborative mindset prioritizing team success over individual accolades.
  • Passion for working in an iterative development environment.
  • Ability to solve complex problems using divergent thinking resulting in innovative solutions.
  • Authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Technical athleticism:

  • An ability to break down complex initiatives into simple systems.
  • Evaluate and recommend tools, technologies, and processes to ensure the continuous improvement of software systems.
  • Deep technical domain knowledge: apps, services, systems, or frameworks
  • Strong knowledge and hands-on experience with a growing set of languages, with experience in JavaScript (especially React and Node), Python, and TypeScript
  • Strong knowledge of the AWS cloud platform and experience working with AWS resources such as Lambda, SNS, SQS, S3, Kinesis, Step Functions, IAM, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, DynamoDB

About Our Process 

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

About Our Benefits and Compensation

College Board offers a competitive benefits and compensation program that attracts top talent looking to make a difference in education. As a self-sustaining non-profit, we believe in compensating employees equitably in relation to each other, their qualifications, their impact, and the relevant market.

The hiring range for a new employee in this position is $220,000to $230,000.

College Board differentiates salaries by location so where you live will narrow the portion of this range in which you can expect a salary. Your salary will be carefullydetermined based on your location, relevant experience, the external labor market, and the pay of College Board employees in similar roles.College Board strives to provide our best offer up front based onthis criteria.

Your salary is only one part of all that College Board offers, including but not limited to:

  • A comprehensive package designed to support the well-being of employees and their families and promote education. Our robust benefits package includes health, dental, and vision insurance, generous paid time off, paid parental leave, fertility benefits, pet insurance, tuition assistance, retirement benefits, and more
  • Recognition of exceptional performance through annual bonuses, salary growth over time through market increases, and opportunities for merit raises and promotions based on increased scope of responsibility
  • A job that matters, a team that cares, and a place to learn, innovate and thrive

​

You can expect to have transparent conversations about benefits and compensation with our recruiters throughout your application process.

About Our Culture 

Our community matters, and we strive to practice and improve our culture daily. Here are some headlines: 

  • We are motivated to positively impact the educational and career trajectories of millions of students a year 
  • We prioritize building a diverse and inclusive team where every employee can thrive, and every voice is heard
  • We welcome staff to join any or all six of our affinity groups: ARISE (Alliance for Asian Retention, Inclusion, Success, and Engagement; DIASPORA (Alliance for Pan-African Success and Achievement); Pride (alliance for LGBTQ+ staff and allies); Resilience (alliance for Native staff and advocates); SALSA (Staff Alliance for Latinx Success and Achievement); and WIN (Women’s Impact Network)
  • We value learning and growth; we offer formal and informal ways to lead through your superpowers, sharpen your strengths, and meet your development goals
  • We offer a transparent approach to promotions and merit raises, annual performance-based bonuses, and how to grow your career here over time
  • Our high-performing engineers work with the latest technologies, so you will be constantly learning and sharpening your skills
  • We have a lot of fun bringing wild ideas to life at Hack Day!

🏠 Modelo de trabajo: 100% remoto con disponibilidad para viajar puntualmente

🔎 Tu misión

Participarás en el diseño y evolución de la arquitectura de datos, definiendo tanto modelos para las aplicaciones como modelos compartidos entre distintos sistemas y dominios de negocio.

Incorporamos un perfil con visión arquitectónica, capaz de comprender los procesos de negocio, analizar los sistemas existentes y diseñar modelos de datos sólidos, coherentes y reutilizables, sin limitarse a reproducir las estructuras actuales.

Tus principales responsabilidades serán:

  • Diseñar y evolucionar modelos de datos lógicos y físicos, alineados con las necesidades del negocio.

  • Definir entidades, claves, relaciones, cardinalidades, catálogos, reglas de integridad e historificación.

  • Diseñar los modelos de datos de las aplicaciones y su integración con los modelos compartidos, garantizando la coherencia y reutilización de la información.

  • Analizar sistemas existentes, especialmente AS400/DB2, identificando estructuras, relaciones, dependencias y reglas de negocio, incluso sin documentación.

  • Analizar datos reales mediante SQL para validar claves, relaciones, granularidad, históricos e inconsistencias.

  • Diseñar e implementar modelos físicos en SQL Server, incluyendo DDL, índices, constraints y scripts de evolución.

  • Definir contratos de datos, mapeos origen-destino y criterios de integración entre sistemas.

  • Participar en el diseño de índices y modelos documentales en Elasticsearch.

  • Documentar modelos, decisiones de diseño y linaje mediante DBML/dbdiagram y herramientas de gobierno como OpenMetadata.

  • Colaborar con equipos técnicos y de negocio para garantizar que los modelos responden a las necesidades funcionales.

💡 ¿Qué ofrecemos?

  • Incorporación a un proyecto tecnológico especializado en arquitectura, modelado y gobierno del dato.

  • Estabilidad y contratación indefinida.

  • Formación continua a través de RDT Academy.

  • Cursos de idiomas para seguir impulsando tu desarrollo profesional.

jobs.title: Patient Access Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Position SummaryAdvantixxRCM is seeking an experienced Patient Access Specialist to support the front end of the revenue cycle for our healthcare clients.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

AdvantixxRCM is seeking an experienced Patient Access Specialist to support the front end of the revenue cycle for our healthcare clients.

This position is responsible for insurance eligibility verification, benefits verification, prior authorization, referral requirements, patient coverage review, and identification of potential reimbursement issues before services are rendered.

The Patient Access Specialist plays an important role in preventing avoidable denials and ensuring healthcare providers have accurate insurance information before treating patients.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Verify patient insurance eligibility before scheduled services.
  • Confirm active coverage and effective dates.
  • Verify patient demographics and insurance information.
  • Verify primary and secondary insurance coverage.
  • Identify coordination-of-benefits issues.
  • Verify provider participation/network status when appropriate.
  • Review payer-specific requirements.
  • Determine whether prior authorization is required.
  • Determine whether a referral is required.
  • Submit prior authorization requests.
  • Obtain and submit supporting clinical documentation as required.
  • Follow up with insurance companies regarding pending authorization requests.
  • Track authorization status through determination.
  • Document authorization numbers, effective dates, approved services/units, and expiration dates.
  • Monitor existing authorizations to prevent expiration or exhaustion of approved visits/units.
  • Coordinate referral requirements.
  • Communicate authorization or eligibility problems to the client before services whenever possible.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of all verification and authorization activities.

Benefits Verification

The Patient Access Specialist may verify:

  • Deductibles
  • Copayments
  • Coinsurance
  • Out-of-pocket amounts
  • Coverage limitations
  • Service-specific benefits
  • Visit limitations
  • Authorization requirements
  • Referral requirements
  • Network requirements
  • Primary/secondary payer information

The employee must accurately document information obtained from payer portals or insurance representatives and avoid representing benefit verification as a guarantee of payment.

Prior Authorization

Responsibilities include:

  • Determine whether authorization is required.
  • Initiate authorization requests.
  • Submit required documentation.
  • Communicate with payer utilization management departments.
  • Follow up on pending authorizations.
  • Track authorization decisions.
  • Document authorization/reference numbers.
  • Track approved CPT/services when applicable.
  • Track approved visits or units.
  • Track authorization effective and expiration dates.
  • Request extensions or additional visits when appropriate.
  • Escalate authorization denials requiring clinical review or appeal.
  • Notify the appropriate client/team when services are not authorized.

Denial Prevention

A major responsibility of this position is preventing avoidable denials before claims are submitted.

The Patient Access Specialist should identify potential issues involving:

  • Inactive insurance
  • Incorrect member information
  • Incorrect payer
  • Coordination of benefits
  • Missing prior authorization
  • Expired authorization
  • Exhausted visits/units
  • Missing referral
  • Out-of-network provider
  • Service exclusions
  • Benefit limitations
  • Incorrect provider/service location information

Issues should be communicated promptly to the appropriate client or AdvantixxRCM department.

Internal Coordination

The Patient Access Specialist works closely with the:

Medical Billing Specialist for claim-related insurance information.

A/R Specialist for eligibility-related unpaid claims.

Denial Management Specialist for authorization and eligibility denials.

Credentialing Specialist for provider participation/enrollment concerns.

Client Account Manager for information needed from healthcare clients.

Operations Manager for escalated issues and payer trends.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 1–2 years of healthcare insurance verification, prior authorization, medical billing, patient access, or RCM experience preferred.
  • Experience verifying insurance eligibility and benefits.
  • Experience obtaining prior authorizations.
  • Familiarity with Medicare, Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, and commercial insurance.
  • Experience using insurance payer portals.
  • Understanding of healthcare insurance terminology.
  • Knowledge of deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket responsibilities.
  • Strong organizational and follow-up skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Strong written and verbal communication.
  • Ability to manage multiple pending authorizations and deadlines simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous RCM or medical billing company experience.
  • Experience with multiple healthcare specialties.
  • Experience with Availity and other payer portals.
  • Familiarity with CPT/HCPCS terminology.
  • Experience working with Medicare and Medicaid.
  • Experience handling referrals.
  • Experience with medical necessity documentation.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus.

Performance Expectations

Performance will be evaluated based on:

  • Eligibility verification accuracy
  • Prior authorization completion
  • Authorization turnaround
  • Follow-up timeliness
  • Documentation accuracy
  • Authorization tracking
  • Prevention of eligibility/authorization-related denials
  • Productivity
  • Client communication
  • Compliance with payer requirements

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who understands that successful revenue cycle management begins before the claim is submitted.

The Patient Access Specialist should proactively identify insurance, eligibility, authorization, and referral issues so they can be addressed before they become denials or lost revenue.

We need someone who takes ownership of pending authorizations and does not consider the job finished simply because an authorization request was submitted.

Why Join AdvantixxRCM?

AdvantixxRCM is building a comprehensive revenue cycle organization focused on improving reimbursement while preventing avoidable revenue loss for healthcare providers.

We value accuracy, accountability, urgency, communication, and problem-solving.

Job Description

This is a full-time remote position that can be located anywhere in the U.S

The Principal Data Platform Engineer, Snowflake is the platform administrator and technical lead for Enlyte's Snowflake environment and its supporting tooling.   • Serve as the technical point of contact for the Snowflake vendor relationship, including support cases, roadmap, and new feature evaluation

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience administering Snowflake in a production enterprise environment

  • Strong cloud engineering experience, primarily AWS, including the services that integrate with Snowflake

  • Experience with dbt, Airflow, or similar data orchestration and transformation tools
  • Experience in insurance, claims, healthcare, or financial services technology environments
  • Experience with organizational transformation from project-based to product/service delivery models

Description

About Factify

AI agents are starting to make decisions in regulated enterprises, including US banks and insurers. Factify turns an organization's policies, documents and real-world practice into a sealed, executable rulebook that governs how those agents decide. Every decision is traceable, auditable and ratified by the people who own the process.

The role

You will be our US insurance expert. You will map how critical decisions are really made inside US carriers, starting with how claims are adjudicated and how coverage is interpreted, and turn that judgment into explicit, testable rules. Those rules need to hold up with adjusters, auditors and state regulators. As our work expands, you will cover more of the carrier's critical processes.

What you'll do

  • Map claims processes end to end: first notice of loss, triage, coverage verification, investigation, adjudication, reserving, settlement and recovery.
  • Map other critical insurance processes as customer needs arise, using your own experience of how they run in practice.
  • Analyze policy forms, endorsements, exclusions and claims manuals. Identify contradictions and ambiguity between documents and between documents and practice.
  • Translate coverage interpretation and authority limits into structured rules, including SIU and fraud indicators, escalation triggers and state-mandated handling timelines.
  • Build test cases and golden-label datasets (covered / not covered / refer, with evidence) across lines such as property, auto, health and liability.
  • Review agent outputs against how experienced insurance professionals would decide, and document the failure modes.
  • Work with customer leaders to ratify and maintain the rulebook over time.

Requirements

  • 10+ years in insurance at a US carrier, TPA or MGA, with deep expertise in claims management, claims operations, coverage analysis or insurance compliance.
  • Deep understanding of policy structure, exclusions, conditions and subrogation, and of US insurance regulation: state unfair claims settlement practices, NAIC model laws, and state department of insurance requirements.
  • Experience with process documentation, quality assurance or audit of insurance decisions.
  • The ability to separate what the policy says from what the organization actually does, and to explain both clearly.
  • Availability for regular overlap with our Tel Aviv team.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with insurance leaders, executives and engineers.
  • Location: Remote (US), with regular overlap with our Tel Aviv team (US Eastern morning hours).

Strong advantage

Hands-on experience in any critical process inside an insurer. Every additional process you know from the inside widens the range of customer problems you can solve. Examples:

  • Underwriting and risk selection
  • Policy administration, endorsements and renewals
  • Billing, premium collection and cancellations
  • Fraud detection and SIU investigations
  • Subrogation, salvage and recovery
  • Reinsurance and ceded claims
  • Reserving and actuarial processes
  • Regulatory filings, market conduct and compliance
  • Broker and agent management
  • Customer service, complaints and litigation management

Nice to have

  • Experience at an insurtech, in a claims-automation program or in a Big 4 insurance practice.
  • Exposure to rules engines, core insurance platforms (such as Guidewire) or AI governance.
  • CPCU, AIC, ARM or equivalent credentials.

jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Reports to: Head of People

Level: Director

Location: Remote, but in a location that allows for at least ~3 hours of daily overlap with East Africa Time, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. At this stage of GiveDirectly’s growth and scale, we’re prioritizing hiring in the countries below, where we can employ you through a GD entity or an established employer of record: Cameroon, Canada, Colombia, DRC, Germany, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Netherlands, Nigeria, Poland, Portugal, Rwanda, South Africa, Spain, Turkey, Uganda, United Kingdom, and United States. This list reflects where our employment infrastructure is established today, and may evolve as we grow. If you’re based elsewhere and not open to relocation, we may not be able to consider your application for this role right now, but we’d encourage you to check back. Please note that we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment Visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

Travel: Approximately 3-4 trips per year, including at least one to a country of operation and one to a key in-person leadership moment.

About this role

We are currently planning for a significant increase in scale, and we are building the People function that can carry it.

This is our first senior talent management role. Today we have pieces of talent management programs and processes in place, but not yet a function. You will build one: an intentional approach to how we onboard, develop, and retain our people. That covers performance management and its link to pay, manager and leadership development, learning, onboarding, talent planning and succession, employee listening and engagement, and culture and values.

The first year is weighted toward four priorities: joining the redesign of our performance system early, alongside the Head of People, and owning it as it moves into execution, as we move to pay for performance, revamping onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring, planning our values retreat for senior leaders, and getting a read on employee listening and engagement. As those take shape, the balance shifts toward the longer-term build: the vision and roadmap for the function, a foundational manager program, talent planning and succession, and the team around you.

The reason for this weight: the performance system and onboarding are our most acute gaps today, but they should not be construed as a ceiling of the job. We are hiring a senior talent management leader who can shape the whole function over several years, not the owner of one or two programs. If your instinct on reading this is that the performance redesign is the whole job, this role probably isn’t the right fit, and the reverse is also true: if you want to set strategy but not build the first versions yourself, year one will frustrate you.

What you’ll do

Build the talent management function

  • Within your first 90 days, assess what exists today across these areas, recommend the sequencing for the first year, and agree to it with the Head of People.
  • Set the vision and multi-year roadmap for talent management across the areas it covers, and sequence the work against the People roadmap.
  • Propose the team around it, and decide what we build in-house and what we buy or borrow.
  • Connect talent management to workforce planning, compensation, and recruitment, in partnership with the Head of People, Finance, and function leaders.

Own the performance system

  • Join the performance system redesign early, alongside the Head of People, and own it as it moves into execution: a system that produces reliable, calibrated outputs to inform merit increases, connected to our new salary bands.
  • Make the system worth using, not a check-the-box exercise: one that helps managers hold better performance and development conversations and gives employees clarity on expectations, feedback, and growth.
  • Build calibration and the data around it so ratings and merit decisions stay consistent and fair across countries, currencies, and manager quality.
  • Set a clear global standard for handling low performance that doesn’t default to a misconduct process, and equip managers to use it.
  • Iterate the system through multiple cycles, using calibration, outcome data, and feedback from managers and employees to improve it.

Build how people join, learn, and are led

  • Revamp onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring: own the content and experience for new hires and their managers, working with People Ops on process and systems.
  • Build a foundational manager program and the tools behind it: feedback, coaching, difficult conversations, and performance management.
  • Extend into leadership development and broader learning as the function matures.

Shape culture and listen to employees

  • Plan the values retreat with an external facilitator and our executive sponsor, and own what carries into daily work afterward.
  • Get a read on listening and engagement today, covering what we hear, where it goes, and what should change, and use it to build our employee listening strategy.
  • Stand up talent planning and succession as the organization matures.

What this role is not

  • Not a recruiting role. Hiring sits with our Talent Acquisition team. You partner with them on the handoff into onboarding and on how we assess and develop talent once people are here.
  • Not the owner of compensation design. Pay structures and bands are set through our compensation work. You own how performance is assessed and how ratings connect to pay decisions.
  • Not an employee relations or casework role. Cases in country belong to managers and HR Managers, supported by the People team. You own the performance system and the manager capability that helps them handle concerns well.
  • Not the owner of HR systems or process administration. Onboarding workflows and our HRIS sit with People Ops. You own the content and the experience.

Who we’re looking for

Required

  • 7+ years in talent management, performance, or organizational design roles, including time leading a function or a major part of one.
  • You have designed a performance system, not only administered one. You can show how ratings connected to pay and what you changed after the first cycle.
  • You have kept a rating and pay system fair across contexts with different currencies, labor markets, and manager quality.
  • You are a hands-on builder. You have built talent management programs and systems from scratch, or close to it, in a start-up or scale-up: performance, onboarding, manager development, or a whole function, where what you needed did not exist and you built it while the volume was already arriving. We are not looking for steady-state operating experience, or for leaders who have overseen this work without building it themselves.
  • You think in systems. You can show how a change in one part of a talent system, such as ratings, calibration, pay, promotion, or onboarding, shows up in the others, and you reason from the underlying problem rather than copying another organization’s template.
  • You design with change management in mind from the start. You plan for how managers and employees in different countries and cultures will adopt a new program or system as part of the design, not as a rollout step afterward, and can show how you knew it stuck rather than being worked around.
  • You have deep experience in at least two of onboarding, manager development, and employee engagement or listening, and working experience in the third. You have built programs and content people actually used, and can show how you knew they worked.
  • A track record of joining a major project already in motion, taking it over, and working through disagreement with a senior partner, and of influencing without formal authority in a matrixed organization.
  • Judgment and prioritization. You decide what slips and say so plainly.

Preferred

  • Experience in a mission-driven or international organization, ideally alongside high-growth commercial or tech experience.
  • Experience working across multiple countries, including sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience working with external facilitators, consultants, or vendors, and knowing what to hand off and what to hold.
  • Comfort using data (survey, performance, calibration) to make decisions, and knowing when the numbers mislead.
  • Exposure to compensation design or close work with a total rewards team.
  • Professional French or Portuguese.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income. Commitment to Safeguarding

jobs.excerpt: About SERHANT. SERHANT.  is the most followed real estate brand globally, redefining the traditional brokerage model through media, content, and innovation.
jobs.description:
About SERHANT.

SERHANT. is the most followed real estate brand globally, redefining the traditional brokerage model through media, content, and innovation. Powered by a full-service in-house film studio and amplification platform, we position our properties - and our agents - in front of more people than anyone else.

About the Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented Transaction Specialist to play a crucial role in ensuring smooth, compliant transactions across our team. In this role, you will manage transaction workflows end-to-end, including document compliance, commission processing, and agent support.

You will serve as a key partner to agents, guiding them through systems, processes, and requirements while ensuring accuracy and timeliness at every stage of the transaction lifecycle. This role requires a strong understanding of compliance, financial accuracy, and internal systems, along with the ability to proactively identify issues and drive solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Transaction & Compliance Management
    • Review, audit, and manage transaction files to ensure compliance with brokerage and state-specific requirements
    • Maintain accuracy across all deal stages, demonstrating a strong understanding of transaction statuses and workflows
    • Identify and resolve missing or incorrect documentation that may delay closing or commission processing
    • Independently complete compliance reviews within SkySlope, ensuring files meet all required standards
    • Apply a deep understanding of company policies, regional requirements, and escalation paths (including Broker of Record involvement)
  • Commission Processing & Financial Accuracy
    • Queue, review, and process commissions with a high degree of accuracy and accountability
    • Audit commission structures including splits, referral fees, transaction fees, and co-broke agreements. Strong understanding of team structures and dynamics.
    • Identify and flag discrepancies such as missing splits, deposit mismatches, and incorrect GCI calculations
    • Validate commission data against compliance documentation and financial records
    • Generate CDAs, support escrow release processes, and ensure proper payment readiness
  • Agent Support & Communication
    • Serve as a primary point of contact for agents, providing timely and accurate support on transaction status, submissions, and payment timelines
    • Proactively communicate with agents to resolve outstanding items required to close transactions
    • Manage and respond to a shared inbox, ensuring all assigned communications are addressed by end of day
    • Tag and route inquiries appropriately across internal teams based on ownership and subject matter
  • Systems & Process Expertise
    • Act as a subject matter expert in transaction and commission platforms, including Total Brokerage and SkySlope
    • Maintain detailed notes within transaction records, documenting agent communications and internal escalations
    • Utilize internal tools such as deposit logs to investigate pending funds and transaction discrepancies
  • Operational Excellence & Workflow Optimization
    • Manage a high volume of transactions across multiple stages
    • Self-prioritize tasks and operate independently with minimal oversight in a fast-paced environment
    • Demonstrate strong attention to detail and accuracy aligned with internal quality thresholds
    • Identify inefficiencies in workflows and proactively implement scalable improvements
    • Collaborate cross-functionally with Agent Finance, Accounting, and Brokerage Operations
    • Support ongoing training and knowledge-sharing initiatives to improve team efficiency and agent experience
  • *The company reserves the right to add or change duties at any time.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related field preferred.
  • 3-5 years of experience processing real estate transactions.
  • SkySlope experience preferred.
  • Experience with real estate transactions in Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, New England, and Virginia
  • Real Estate license a plus.
  • Preference given to candidates based in Eastern and Central time zones.

Skills

  • Exceptional attention to detail in auditing documents and financial data
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • High level of customer service and responsiveness
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel (pivot tables, lookups, etc.)
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Ability to quickly learn new systems and adapt to evolving processes
  • Self-starter with the ability to work independently and drive results

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location.

The national base pay range for this position within the United States is $70,000.00 - $75,000.00 USD.

Benefits

Eligible employees may receive medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off and paid holidays; retirement benefits; and other company-sponsored benefits, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and plan terms.

Your Location

This position is remote eligible for candidates based in Eastern and Central time zones. The role may include occasional work at additional SERHANT. offices or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. Candidates must live within the United States.

Hiring Statement

SERHANT. is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination or harassment. We expect every member of the SERHANT. community to do their part to cultivate and maintain an environment where everyone has the opportunity to feel included and is afforded the respect and dignity they deserve.

Decisions related to hiring, compensating, training, evaluating performance, or terminating are made fairly, and we provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified candidates and staff. We examine our unconscious biases and take responsibility for always striving to create an inclusive environment that makes every employee and candidate feel welcome.

Recruiting Fraud Notice

Please be aware that fictitious job openings, consulting engagements, solicitations, or employment offers may be circulated on the Internet in an attempt to obtain privileged information, or to prompt you to pay a fee for services related to recruitment or training.

SERHANT. does not charge any application, processing, or training fee at any stage of the recruiting or hiring process. All genuine job openings will be posted here on on our Careers page or Linkedin, and all communications from the SERHANT. recruiting team and/or hiring managers will be from an @serhant.com email address.

Visa Sponsorship Notice

Thank you for your interest in working with us! At this time, we are not able to offer H-1B visa or any other work authorization sponsorship. To be considered for any of our open roles, candidates must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

With an A+ BBB Rating and a Trustpilot “Excellent” score (as of Sept. 16, 2025)*, we are proud to be redefining the industry for our members and our team alike.

The Role

We’re hiring a Director of Web & Conversion Optimization to own the strategy, design, and performance of our website and landing pages. Sitting at the intersection of brand, product marketing, media, and web engineering, you’ll build a digital storefront that reflects our brand, delivers a best-in-class user experience, and drives a qualified, high-intent pipeline. You’ll lead a website transformation including an end-to-end redesign, ownership of the ongoing roadmap, and continual optimization for search and conversion.

  • Strategic Website Leadership: Direct content strategy, oversee testing frameworks, and drive high-level strategic updates across our entire site. Lead the strategic rollout and launch of the remainder of our website before EOY, building upon our successful new homepage launch.

Work closely with performance and organic marketing leads to design, tailor, and optimize landing page experiences from top-of-funnel (e.g., Instagram video, paid search,etc.) and nurture campaigns ensuring distinct best practices are applied to drive maximum revenue and conversion.
  • Search Visibility (SEO/AEO/GEO): Own on-site search optimization across traditional and AI-driven search. Ensure the site’s structure, content architecture, and technical foundation are built so Facet ranks in search engines and is cited and surfaced by answer engines and generative AI platforms, partnering with the Content team on the editorial strategy that feeds it.
  • E-commerce Strategy & Build: Define and lead Facet’s path to e-commerce, from strategy through execution. Design the transactional journeys, infrastructure, and optimization practices that let members discover, select, and purchase directly on-site, laying the foundation for a scalable, self-serve growth channel.

  • Platform, Performance & Accessibility: Partner with Engineering to set the direction for the website platform — CMS, tooling, and infrastructure — and own the standards the site must meet for speed, reliability, mobile performance, and accessibility (WCAG). jobs.description:
How we work ?
Ofelia Perks & Benefits
About the role

We are building our cloud offering to a full SaaS model, and building a new Architecture team to lead that shift.

You'll partner closely with our Head of Architecture on the software-and-cloud vision, and work day to day with the Cloud/DevOps and Platform teams. You'll have real ownership over how we build, secure, and scale the platform as it grows from where it is today toward a multi-tenant, multi-customer product.

How we work -Architecture built together

This role comes with real autonomy, on purpose. Our Head of Architecture will be closely involved at the start, introducing you to the teams and setting direction, and will then step back to let you drive your own scope. We're not looking for someone to manage closely; we're looking for someone who can take a blank page and own it, and who knows when to loop others in.

The Architecture team itself is still taking shape, so a lot of how we work will be built together with you. In practice, that means direct, frequent exchanges with the teams below rather than layers of process, closer to mentorship and architecture review than top-down direction:

  • Head of Architecture (hiring manager) : software & AI architecture, partnering for a unified product vision

  • Cloud/DevOps team : daily collaboration and mentoring

  • Platform team : cross-cutting architecture topics

  • Information Security Officer : validating cloud security choices

The day-to-day job

Day to day, you'll own the cloud side of that transition end to end:

  • Design and evolve the platform's multi-tenant cloud architecture (tenant isolation, data models, onboarding flows), robust, scalable, and secure, with AWS as the primary provider and a second cloud provider

  • Define and promote architecture best practices: high availability, resilience, cost optimization (FinOps)

  • Lead containerization and orchestration with Kubernetes (cluster design, networking, security, observability, lifecycle management)

  • Industrialize provisioning and deployments through Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and CI/CD pipelines (GitOps)

  • Integrate and operationalize generative AI services, notably Amazon Bedrock (model selection, RAG, AI usage governance)

  • Own the cloud security architecture, in partnership with our Information Security Officer, who covers ISO 27001/SOC 2 compliance: IAM, encryption, network segmentation, cluster hardening, threat modeling

  • Define operational resilience practices: disaster recovery (RTO/RPO), backup strategy, SLA/SLO

  • Mentor and upskill the DevOps and engineering teams

  • Maintain active technology watch and challenge existing architecture choices

What success looks like

30 days: Understand and diagnose

  • You've completed a full audit of the current platform: Kubernetes setup (shared cluster, namespace-per-tenant), network, IaC and CI/CD maturity, and you've mapped the gaps against a production-grade SaaS (HA, horizontal scalability, WAF, observability).

  • You've built working relationships with the Cloud/DevOps and Platform teams and established a lightweight architecture review ritual with them.

  • You share a prioritized diagnosis with the Head of Architecture: what's solid, what's at risk, what blocks our first customer.

60 days : Define the target and unblock

  • The target multi-tenant architecture is documented and validated: tenant isolation model, HA strategy, horizontal scaling approach, and the security baseline (including WAF).

  • The IaC and GitOps roadmap is defined, and the first components are managed through Terraform and automated pipelines.

  • You've identified the integration pattern for generative AI services (Amazon Bedrock) and validated it with the Platform team.

90 days : Execute toward our first customer

  • The critical gaps for production readiness (HA, scalability, WAF) are either resolved or scheduled with clear owners and dates.

  • A production-readiness checklist for onboarding our first SaaS customer is defined and agreed with the teams, you own the architecture sign-off.

  • Teams are progressively upskilled: architecture decisions are documented (ADRs), and the DevOps team is autonomous on the new IaC foundations.

The person we're looking for

We're not looking for an architect by training who's only ever advised from the outside. The person who thrives here has likely grown into architecture from a hands-on DevOps or backend engineering background, someone who's done the "run" before stepping into design, and who's comfortable in organizations where roles aren't siloed.

Experience & certifications:

Senior experience in cloud architecture and infrastructure, including several years in critical production environments

  • Hands-on experience taking a SaaS product to production from its early stages

  • AWS certification required (Solutions Architect Professional preferred)

Technical skills:

  • Deep Kubernetes expertise: cluster architecture, Helm, operators, service mesh, security (RBAC, network policies, admission controllers)

  • Strong automation background: Terraform (essential), Ansible, CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD)

  • Multi-tenant architecture: tenant isolation, data modeling, onboarding flows

  • Operational resilience: disaster recovery (RTO/RPO), backup strategy, SLA/SLO definition

  • Data layer: managed databases, storage, and data migration

  • Cloud-native security: IAM, secrets management, encryption, audit practices (in partnership with our security team on ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR)

  • Solid grasp of microservices architecture, networking (VPC, DNS, load balancing), and observability (Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch...)

  • Cost-conscious cloud engineering (FinOps): cost optimization and budget governance

  • Comfort integrating generative AI services in production (e.g., Amazon Bedrock or equivalent). Deep Bedrock experience is a strong plus

  • Daily, hands-on use of AI-assisted coding tools

Nice-to-have:

  • Certification on a second cloud provider (Azure, GCP)

  • Familiarity with EU data residency/sovereignty requirements (relevant given GDPR compliance and sovereign cloud options)

  • AI-assisted intelligent monitoring and alerting

Soft skills

  • Ability to make complex technical topics accessible to varied audiences

  • Technical leadership and genuine appetite for mentoring

  • Pragmatism and comfortable getting hands-on operationally when needed, without staying there

  • Autonomy and rigor ability to move forward without constant supervision in a team that's still taking shape

  • Professional French and English

Hiring process

Our process is designed to move quickly, give you full visibility at every stage, and make the best use of your time.

  1. Screening call with HR (45 min)

  2. Interview with the hiring manager (1h)

  3. Live technical role play interview (1h)

  4. Final interview with CHRO (1h)

jobs.description:
Clinical Research Project Manager – Study Start-Up & Site Activation

Company: UniTriTeam (UTT)
Position: Clinical Research Project Manager – Study Start-Up
Department: Clinical Research Operations
Employment Type: Full-Time
Location: Remote / Client-Specific Requirements

Position Overview

UniTriTeam is seeking a highly organized, proactive, and results-driven Clinical Research Project Managerto support one of our clinical research clients in managing the end-to-end study start-up process.

This individual will be responsible for coordinating cross-functional teams, managing timelines, tracking critical deliverables, and ensuring clinical research studies are activated on time, with all operational, regulatory, contractual, and system requirements in place.

The ideal candidate has a strong clinical research background, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and brings exceptional attention to detail, urgency, accountability, and follow-through.

We are looking for someone who doesn't just track progress—they drive it. This person must anticipate roadblocks, take initiative, hold stakeholders accountable, and ensure that nothing falls through the cracks.

This is a highly visible, hands-on role requiring strong project management skills, clinical research knowledge, and the ability to coordinate multiple priorities and stakeholders simultaneously.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Study Start-Up & Site Activation
  • Own and manage the study start-up process from initial study award or feasibility through site activation and readiness for first patient enrollment.
  • Develop comprehensive study start-up plans, timelines, milestones, and deliverables for each assigned study.
  • Coordinate start-up activities across regulatory, contracts, budgets, clinical operations, finance, recruitment, technology, and other functional teams.
  • Track all required study start-up activities, including feasibility, regulatory submissions, IRB approvals, contracts, budgets, training, system readiness, and sponsor requirements.
  • Ensure all study-specific documentation, approvals, and operational requirements are completed before site activation.
  • Identify critical-path activities, dependencies, and potential delays, implementing proactive mitigation plans.
  • Drive timely completion of start-up milestones while maintaining compliance and quality standards.
  1. Cross-Functional Project Management
  • Serve as the central point of coordination across internal departments, external sponsors, CROs, vendors, and site leadership.
  • Lead study start-up meetings, establish clear action items, assign owners, and ensure timely follow-through.
  • Create accountability across functional teams by clearly communicating responsibilities, deadlines, and expectations.
  • Proactively identify gaps in communication, handoffs, or ownership and resolve them before they impact timelines.
  • Escalate risks, delays, and unresolved issues with recommended solutions and recovery plans.
  • Maintain strong working relationships with clinical research teams while driving urgency and execution.
  • Ensure all stakeholders have visibility into study progress, priorities, risks, and upcoming milestones.
  1. Timeline, Milestone & Deliverable Management
  • Build and maintain detailed project plans and study start-up trackers.
  • Monitor milestone completion, deliverable status, and readiness across all active studies.
  • Establish realistic timelines and proactively manage competing priorities.
  • Identify bottlenecks and take immediate action to keep projects on schedule.
  • Provide accurate, timely, and actionable status reporting to leadership and stakeholders.
  • Maintain centralized documentation of project decisions, risks, action items, and dependencies.
  • Ensure timely escalation when deliverables are at risk, including clear corrective actions and ownership.
  1. Operational Readiness & Quality
  • Coordinate with relevant teams to ensure studies are operationally ready for activation, including staffing, training, supplies, systems, and required documentation.
  • Verify readiness of applicable clinical research platforms, including CTMS, eRegulatory, eSource, EDC, and other study-specific systems.
  • Ensure that required study start-up processes and documentation align with applicable GCP, regulatory requirements, sponsor expectations, and organizational SOPs.
  • Support effective handoffs from study start-up to ongoing clinical research operations.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve handoffs, standardize processes, and reduce study activation timelines.
  • Maintain a high standard of accuracy, completeness, and quality across all assigned projects.
  1. Stakeholder Communication & Reporting
  • Provide concise, structured updates on study status, milestones, risks, and next steps.
  • Communicate proactively rather than waiting for stakeholders to request updates.
  • Facilitate productive meetings with documented decisions, owners, and due dates.
  • Establish clear expectations with functional leaders and team members.
  • Professionally challenge missed deadlines, unclear ownership, and incomplete deliverables.
  • Serve as a trusted partner to client leadership by demonstrating ownership, reliability, and sound judgment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in life sciences, healthcare administration, clinical research, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of experience in clinical research, preferably within clinical trial operations, site operations, or study start-up.
  • Demonstrated experience managing clinical research projects, study start-up activities, or site activation processes.
  • Strong understanding of the clinical trial lifecycle, particularly feasibility, regulatory requirements, IRB submissions, contracts, budgets, and site activation.
  • Experience coordinating multiple functional departments and managing interdependent deliverables.
  • Strong knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), clinical research regulations, and standard operating procedures.
  • Proficiency with project management tools, trackers, Microsoft Excel, and collaborative platforms.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple studies or projects simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working within a clinical research site, site network, SMO, CRO, or sponsor organization.
  • Direct experience managing multiple study activations concurrently.
  • Familiarity with CTMS, eRegulatory, eSource, and EDC platforms such as CRIO, Clinical Conductor, RealTime, Florence, or comparable systems.
  • Experience developing study start-up dashboards, standardized trackers, and operational performance reports.
  • PMP, ACRP, SOCRA, or other relevant professional certification.
  • Experience improving clinical research workflows and reducing study start-up cycle times.

Critical Success Attributes

We place significant emphasis on how this individual works, not just their technical qualifications.

Exceptionally Organized & Detail-Oriented

  • Maintains meticulous trackers, documentation, and action items.
  • Consistently follows through on commitments.
  • Manages multiple moving pieces without losing visibility into details.
  • Creates structure and clarity in complex or ambiguous environments.

Proactive & Self-Directed

  • Takes initiative without waiting for direction.
  • Anticipates issues and acts before they become problems.
  • Brings solutions and recommendations rather than simply identifying obstacles.
  • Demonstrates strong ownership of outcomes.

Accountable & Results-Driven

  • Treats deadlines as commitments.
  • Holds themselves and others accountable.
  • Takes responsibility for moving work forward, even when deliverables depend on other teams.
  • Remains focused on successful, on-time study activation.

Strong Cross-Functional Leader

  • Confidently coordinates teams and stakeholders without requiring direct reporting authority.
  • Communicates clearly, directly, and professionally.
  • Is comfortable following up, challenging delays, and escalating when necessary.
  • Builds collaborative relationships while maintaining urgency and accountability.

Thrives in a Fast-Paced Environment

  • Comfortably manages competing priorities and changing timelines.
  • Remains composed, focused, and organized under pressure.
  • Adapts quickly while maintaining a high standard of execution.
  • Demonstrates a strong sense of urgency and continuous improvement.

Key Performance Indicators / Measures of Success

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • On-Time Study Activation: Percentage of studies activated by the committed target date.
  • Milestone Adherence: Percentage of study start-up milestones completed on schedule.
  • Critical Deliverable Completion: Timely completion of required regulatory, contractual, operational, and system-readiness activities.
  • Risk Identification & Resolution: Proactive identification, escalation, and resolution of issues impacting study timelines.
  • Project Visibility & Accountability: Accuracy and completeness of study trackers, reporting, and action-item management.
  • Cross-Functional Effectiveness: Ability to drive timely decisions, remove bottlenecks, and maintain alignment across teams.
  • Continuous Improvement: Demonstrated improvements in start-up processes, coordination, and activation cycle times.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 90 days, the successful candidate will have established strong relationships with key stakeholders, gained a clear understanding of the client's study start-up processes, and assumed ownership of assigned study timelines and deliverables.

They will demonstrate the ability to independently lead cross-functional meetings, maintain accurate project tracking, proactively identify risks, and drive accountability across departments.

Most importantly, leadership should have confidence that every assigned study is being actively managed, potential delays are identified early, and nothing is falling through the cracks.

About UniTriTeam

UniTriTeam (UTT) partners with clinical research organizations to provide specialized operational, regulatory, technology, and project management support. Our team helps clients improve efficiency, strengthen execution, and scale clinical research operations through experienced professionals and practical, results-driven solutions.

We are committed to delivering exceptional service, operational excellence, and measurable results for our clients.

jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: Junior Staff Accountant

POSITION CLASSIFICATION: Associate

SALARY BAND: B

REPORTS TO: Director, Finance & Accounting

LOCATION: Remote

About American Rivers

American Rivers is a national conservation organization working to make every river clean and healthy for people and wildlife. We combine evidence-based solutions with enduring partnerships to safeguard the 4.4 million miles of rivers and streams that are essential to our nation’s clean drinking water, extraordinary wildlife, and the strength of our communities. For more than 50 years, our staff, supporters, and partners have been driven by a common belief: Life Depends on Rivers.

The beauty of rivers is that they connect all people and communities – including within our organization. The life experiences, knowledge, innovation, and talent that different people bring to our work provides perspectives, experiences, and competencies which are critical to our effectiveness in protecting wild rivers, restoring damaged rivers, and conserving clean water for people and nature.

JOB SUMMARY

The Junior Staff Accountant provides support to the Finance and Accounting team to ensure that American Rivers’ accounting functions are performed in accordance with GAAP and organizational guidelines and that transactions are recorded in a timely manner.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Accounts Payable (A/P): (25%)
    • Process vendor invoices accurately and promptly, ensuring proper approvals and coding.
    • Verify that all expenditures are properly authorized and supported with appropriate documentation.
    • Maintain detailed documentation and audit trails for all federal award transactions.
    • Prepare and process electronic payments, ACH transfers, and check disbursements.
    • Vendor File Maintenance:
      • Verify and collect required documentation from all vendors, including W-9 forms, executed contracts, and proof of insurance where applicable.
      • Review vendor information for accuracy before activation and regularly update vendor data (e.g., addresses, tax IDs, banking details).
      • Ensure vendor setup complies with internal control policies, procurement standards, and federal grant regulations under OMB Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200).
  • Accounts Receivable (A/R): (25%)
    • Record and reconcile incoming payments, including grant reimbursements, donor contributions, and other receivables.
    • Prepare and submit invoices to funding agencies and clients in accordance with contract and grant requirements.
    • Track outstanding receivables and follow up on delayed payments or discrepancies.
    • Process and record all federal award drawdowns and reimbursements.
  • General Ledger and Reconciliations (25%)
    • Prepare journal entries, adjusting entries, and closing entries as needed.
    • Support month-end and year-end closing processes.
    • Perform regular bank reconciliations and ensure all transactions are accurately reflected in accounting records.
    • Reconcile credit card and balance sheet general ledger accounts monthly.
    • Identify, investigate, and correct discrepancies promptly.
  • Compliance (25%)
    • 1099 Reporting:
      • Prepare and issue annual Form 1099-NEC/MISC to vendors in compliance with IRS regulations.
      • Maintain accurate vendor records to ensure timely and accurate year-end reporting.
    • Audit and Reporting Support:
      • Provide accurate schedules and reconciliations to auditors and management as requested.
      • Assist with annual audits, single audits (if applicable), and other financial reviews.
      • Support the Finance Department in preparing accurate schedules, reports, and grant-related reconciliations.
    • Regulatory and Standards Compliance:
      • Ensure all accounting activities and records comply with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
      • Adhere to all applicable rules and regulations set forth by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and other relevant state and federal authorities.
  • Perform other duties and special projects in support of the department as needed.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field desired. Internship or relevant coursework experience is a plus.
  • Self-motivated, with the ability to work independently and proactively in a remote environment.
  • Well organized with high attention to detail.
  • Ability to take initiative and follow through on assignments with minimal direction.
  • Team player with excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with geographically dispersed colleagues.
  • Ability to multi-task and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including phone, email, and video conferencing.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and Adobe software.
  • Reliable high-speed internet and a dedicated home workspace.
  • Personal commitment to American Rivers’ mission.

Candidates who are unsure if they meet all minimum qualifications or who have transferrable skills and experience beyond the conservation sector are encouraged to apply.

LOCATION

Remote within AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IA, ID, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MT, NC, NM, NY, NV, OH, OR, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA, WI, NY and WY.

COMPENSATION

American Rivers offers marketable compensation that reflects the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate. The salary range for this position is $52,600-$64,200, annually, depending on experience and qualifications. Pay rates are offered in compliance with all applicable state wage and hour regulations. We provide a comprehensive Total Rewards package to our full-time, regular employees, including:

  • Health and Wellness: Medical, dental, vision, long-term and short-term disability, and life insurance.
  • Financial Security: After one year of service, American Rivers begins contributing a 3% employer contribution. There is no vesting schedule for employer contributions as employees are 100% vested upon participation.
  • Time Off: Four weeks of paid leave, eleven paid holidays, three floating holidays, and sick leave.

At American Rivers, we are committed to supporting our employee’s well-being, professional growth, and financial security, ensuring they can thrive both at work and in life.

COMMUNITY AND OPPORTUNITY

  • At American Rivers, our core values drive everything we do – we Lead with Collaboration and Trust, Infuse Equity and Justice, Deliver Results, and Ensure Staff and Volunteers Thrive. We are committed to fostering a workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and empowered to make a difference.
  • Our culture prioritizes work-life thriving through Focus Fridays (no internal meetings), professional development opportunities, a home office stipend and our comprehensive leave policies, including sabbatical leave (every seven years) and paid parental leave (six weeks w/ one year of service).
  • We also ensure leadership stays connected to staff needs through an internal advisory group, fostering open communication and continuous improvement.
  • At American Rivers, our people are our strength, and we are dedicated to building a thriving, inclusive workplace where everyone can grow and contribute to our mission.

American Rivers is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. To request this document in an alternate format or to request reasonable accommodation, please contact the Human Resources department at 202-243-7040 or . Please note that one week’s advance notice is preferred.

Applicant must be legally allowed to work as an employee in the United States.American Rivers is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Candidates of all personal and professional backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Salary: $52,600-$64,200

About Zact

Zact is a fintech innovator dedicated to helping organizations simplify expense and payment management. Our platform aligns employees, finance, and accounting with stronger controls, cleaner workflows, and continuous reconciliation to financial systems.

We partner with banks and other financial institutions to deliver modern commercial card, expense management, accounts payable, travel, and related payment capabilities.

Role Overview

Zact is seeking a Compliance & Risk Manager to own the day-to-day operation of key elements of our compliance program across audit, privacy, and financial-crime oversight.

This is a hands-on role responsible for coordinating Zact's SOC and PCI audits, managing compliance with GDPR and other applicable privacy laws, supporting compliance monitoring and testing, and overseeing Zact's responsibilities related to BSA, AML, and OFAC.

Because Zact distributes its platform through financial institutions, the BSA/AML/OFAC component of the role is primarily focused on monitoring and documenting the compliance activities of our reseller bank partners, confirming that assigned responsibilities are being performed, and supporting related audits, examinations, and due diligence reviews.

This role is not intended to serve as a bank's BSA Officer or perform the bank's core transaction-monitoring function. Instead, the Compliance & Risk Manager will ensure that Zact maintains appropriate oversight, documentation, escalation, and evidence regarding the compliance responsibilities performed by its financial institution partners.

The Compliance & Risk Manager will report to the Chief Compliance Officer and work closely with Security, Legal, Operations, Engineering, Finance, and our bank partners.

Key Responsibilities

SOC and PCI Compliance

  • Coordinate Zact's annual SOC 1 and SOC 2 audit processes, including audit planning, evidence collection, auditor requests, control-owner coordination, and remediation activities.
  • Coordinate PCI DSS assessments and related compliance activities.
  • Maintain audit calendars, evidence repositories, control documentation, and supporting records.
  • Work with internal control owners to ensure required controls are performed and appropriately documented throughout the year.
  • Track audit findings, exceptions, and remediation items through completion.
  • Serve as a primary operational contact for external auditors and assessors.
  • Help maintain continuous audit readiness rather than preparing only at the time of an assessment.

Privacy Compliance

  • Manage Zact's operational compliance with GDPR and other applicable privacy laws and regulations.
  • Maintain and coordinate privacy policies, procedures, data inventories, retention requirements, and supporting documentation.
  • Work with Legal, Security, Engineering, and business teams to incorporate privacy requirements into Zact's products and operations.
  • Coordinate responses to privacy-related customer and bank due diligence requests.
  • Support privacy assessments, audits, and remediation activities.
  • Monitor changes in applicable privacy requirements and coordinate necessary updates to Zact's controls, policies, and procedures.

BSA, AML, and OFAC Oversight

  • Manage Zact's oversight program for BSA, AML, and OFAC activities performed by reseller bank partners.
  • Confirm that applicable bank partners maintain appropriate BSA/AML and OFAC programs and perform the responsibilities assigned to them.
  • Collect and review required certifications, policies, audit reports, testing results, or other evidence from bank partners.
  • Maintain documentation demonstrating Zact's ongoing oversight of reseller bank compliance activities.
  • Identify gaps, exceptions, or missing evidence and coordinate follow-up with the appropriate bank partner and internal stakeholders.
  • Support audits, examinations, and due diligence reviews involving Zact's BSA/AML and OFAC oversight responsibilities.
  • Coordinate with the Chief Compliance Officer on escalation of material compliance issues.

Compliance Monitoring and Risk Management

  • Conduct periodic compliance risk assessments across applicable regulatory and compliance areas.
  • Develop and maintain a risk-based compliance monitoring and testing program.
  • Perform or coordinate periodic testing to confirm that compliance controls are operating as intended.
  • Identify, document, escalate, and track compliance issues through remediation and closure.
  • Monitor changes in applicable laws, regulations, and compliance frameworks and coordinate updates to policies, controls, and procedures.
  • Maintain a clear record of open findings, remediation plans, owners, and target completion dates.

Compliance Program Management

  • Maintain compliance policies, procedures, control documentation, and supporting evidence.
  • Coordinate regulatory, customer, and third-party compliance audits and assessments.
  • Track compliance obligations, testing schedules, findings, remediation plans, and deadlines.
  • Serve as a primary coordinator for bank and prospective customer compliance due diligence requests.
  • Prepare compliance reporting for the Chief Compliance Officer, including open findings, remediation status, upcoming audits, and material compliance risks.
  • Work across the organization to ensure compliance requirements are understood and implemented.
  • Help identify opportunities to improve and automate compliance processes as the company scales.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree required or equivalent experience strongly demonstrating the competency.
  • 5+ years of experience in compliance, risk management, audit, information security compliance, or a related field.
  • Experience working in banking, fintech, payments, or another regulated financial-services environment.
  • Experience coordinating SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or comparable compliance assessments and audits.
  • Hands-on experience managing or supporting compliance with GDPR and/or U.S. privacy laws.
  • Hands-on experience with BSA/AML, OFAC, or financial-crime compliance in a banking, fintech, payments, or financial-services environment.
  • Experience overseeing responsibilities performed by financial institutions, regulated partners, or other third parties.
  • Experience managing audit evidence, control testing, findings, exceptions, and remediation activities.
  • Experience conducting or supporting compliance risk assessments, monitoring, or testing.
  • Ability to work directly with auditors, assessors, financial institutions, and internal control owners.

SAP TM S/4HANA Rollout Consultant, Poland

Contract: 6 months initially, extensible. Long-term programme. Start: 1 November 2026 Location: Remote, for consultants based in Poland. Day rate: EUR 350 a day. Language: English.

The programme

A global manufacturing organisation is moving its transportation processes onto SAP Transportation Management (TM) on S/4HANA. The global template is the base, and it is being rolled out to sites in waves. Each wave brings new plants, new carriers and new country requirements into the template.

You will own the TM solution for the waves you are given. You will run fit-to-standard sessions with the business, decide what the template already covers and what is a real local gap, and design the answer without breaking the global standard. You will then carry that design through build, testing, cutover and early support after go-live.

What you will work on

Fit-gap for each rollout wave. Local transport practice, carriers, legal and document needs measured against the global design. TM solution design on S/4HANA. Freight planning, carrier selection and tendering, freight order execution, charge calculation and freight settlement. Integration across the S/4HANA logistics chain. Outbound sales orders and deliveries, inbound purchasing flows, warehouse execution, and freight cost through to finance. Carrier connectivity. EDI or business network onboarding, tracking, and status messages from carriers. Functional specifications for the build team, working closely with integration, development and test leads. Test planning and defect resolution through integration and user acceptance testing. Cutover, hypercare and handover to support for each wave. Feeding what each wave teaches back into the template, so the next wave starts from a better base.

What you bring

8 or more years in SAP logistics, with SAP TM on S/4HANA as a core part of it. At least one TM rollout or global template programme for a manufacturing business, where you did the fit-gap and the solution design yourself, not only the configuration. Working knowledge of how TM connects to SD, MM, EWM and FI/CO, and where those integrations tend to break. Experience running workshops with business users and turning what they say into a design and a specification. Comfort working remotely across countries in a programme team made up of several companies.

Useful but not essential:

SAP Business Network for Logistics, or a carrier visibility platform. Both embedded and side-by-side TM deployments. Automotive, industrial or process manufacturing. Multimodal, international or dangerous goods transport. SAP TM certification.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent TM rollout: the countries or sites in scope, whether TM was embedded or side-by-side, and what you personally designed.

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced SAP TM people in front of a global manufacturing organisation.
